Using ratio projection, what is the total projected misstatement for the account?
questions.exp: The sampled misstatement rate is $2,000 / $100,000 = 2%, and 2% x $1,500,000 = $30,000. The $5,000 found in the items tested 100% is added without projection, for a total of $35,000. Projecting over the full $2,000,000 gives $40,000, which double-counts the key items.

questions.q: During a substantive test, an auditor finds a large misstatement caused by a one-time system conversion error and believes it is not representative of the population. Under AU-C 530, the auditor may treat it as an anomaly only if
choices: the misstatement occurred in the first month of the year
management represents in writing that the error was isolated
the misstatement is smaller than tolerable misstatement
the auditor obtains a high degree of certainty, through additional procedures, that the misstatement is not representative of the population
questions.exp: AU-C 530 says anomalies arise only in extremely rare circumstances and requires additional procedures giving a high degree of certainty that the misstatement is not representative. Management's representation alone is not sufficient, and the size of the misstatement is not the test.

questions.q: Which of the following procedures constitutes audit sampling under AU-C 530?
choices: Performing a walkthrough of one sales transaction
Selecting 60 items at random from a population of disbursements to project conclusions to the population
Examining all expense items over $50,000 and performing analytical procedures on the remainder
Recalculating every invoice in the population with data analytics software
questions.exp: Audit sampling applies procedures to less than 100% of a population so that every sampling unit has a chance of selection, with the aim of drawing conclusions about the whole population. Testing all key items, a walkthrough, and 100% testing with analytics are not sampling.

questions.q: An auditor uses systematic selection to choose 120 vouchers from a population numbered 1 through 6,000. The random start is voucher 23. What is the number of the second voucher selected?
questions.exp: The sampling interval is 6,000 / 120 = 50, so the selections are 23, 73, 123, and so on. Using the interval itself as the second item, or adding 100 to the start, misapplies the interval.

questions.q: How should tolerable misstatement for a substantive sampling application ordinarily relate to performance materiality?
choices: Tolerable misstatement should exceed overall materiality
Tolerable misstatement should be set equal to the clearly trivial threshold
Tolerable misstatement is ordinarily set at an amount no greater than performance materiality
Tolerable misstatement is unrelated to materiality
questions.exp: AU-C 530 links tolerable misstatement to performance materiality. Tolerable misstatement for a sampling application is ordinarily no greater than performance materiality, to control aggregation risk. Setting it above overall materiality would defeat that purpose.

questions.q: In a substantive test of details, the projected misstatement plus the allowance for sampling risk exceeds tolerable misstatement. Which response is most appropriate?
choices: Ask management to investigate the misstatements and the potential for further misstatement, and consider adjusting the balance, expanding the sample, or performing alternative procedures
Treat all identified misstatements as anomalies
Accept the balance, because the projected misstatement alone is below tolerable misstatement
Reduce the allowance for sampling risk by increasing the acceptable risk of incorrect acceptance after the fact
questions.exp: When the results do not support acceptance, the auditor may request management to investigate and record adjustments, expand testing, or perform other procedures before concluding. Changing risk levels after the results are known to force acceptance would be inappropriate.

questions.q: Before selecting a sample of customer accounts from the accounts receivable subsidiary ledger, the auditor should
choices: confirm all accounts with balances over tolerable misstatement
remove any accounts with credit balances so that the sample is more efficient
obtain management's representation that the ledger is complete
foot the subsidiary ledger and reconcile its total to the general ledger control account
questions.exp: AU-C 530 requires the auditor to determine that the population from which the sample is drawn is appropriate and complete. Footing the ledger and reconciling it to the general ledger does that. Removing credit balances would leave an incomplete population.

questions.q: According to AICPA audit sampling guidance, how should the size of a well-designed nonstatistical sample compare with the size of a statistical sample?
choices: It is determined by the population size alone
It should ordinarily be comparable to the sample size from an efficient statistical sampling application with the same parameters
It may be much smaller, because nonstatistical sampling does not involve sampling risk
It should always be exactly 25 items
questions.exp: Nonstatistical sampling still involves sampling risk, and the same factors (risk, tolerable misstatement, expected misstatement, variability) determine sample size. A well-designed nonstatistical sample is therefore ordinarily comparable in size to an efficient statistical sample.

questions.q: An auditor plans to rely heavily on a control to significantly reduce substantive testing of sales. How should this affect the tolerable deviation rate for the test of that control?
choices: The tolerable rate should be lower
The tolerable rate should equal the expected deviation rate
The tolerable rate should be higher
The tolerable rate is unaffected by the planned degree of reliance
questions.exp: Greater planned reliance means the auditor can accept fewer deviations, so the tolerable rate is set lower, which increases sample size. Setting the tolerable rate equal to the expected rate would make the required sample enormous.

questions.q: For a substantive test of details, an auditor decreases the acceptable risk of incorrect acceptance from 10% to 5% and holds all other factors constant. The effect on the required sample size is that it will
choices: remain the same, because tolerable misstatement did not change
decrease, because a lower risk means fewer errors are expected
decrease, because the auditor is accepting less risk of incorrect rejection
increase, because greater assurance is required
questions.exp: A lower acceptable risk of incorrect acceptance means the auditor wants more confidence, which requires a larger sample. In MUS, for example, the reliability factor for zero misstatements rises from about 2.3 to 3.0. The risk of incorrect rejection is a separate risk.

questions.q: An auditor uses data analytics to recalculate the extension and footing of every sales invoice recorded during the year. Which statement about the risks involved is correct?
choices: Sampling risk does not exist, but nonsampling risk remains, for example from using an incomplete data set
Nonsampling risk is eliminated, but sampling risk remains
Sampling risk is increased because more items are tested
Both sampling risk and nonsampling risk are eliminated
questions.exp: Testing 100% of a population eliminates sampling risk, but nonsampling risk remains, for example if the data set is incomplete or the procedure is misapplied. That is why the auditor still tests the completeness and accuracy of the data used.

questions.q: Before accepting a new audit engagement, a successor auditor obtains the prospective client's permission and makes inquiries of the predecessor auditor under AU-C 210. Which of the following matters is the successor required to include in those inquiries?
choices: The predecessor's assessed level of control risk for each significant account
The predecessor's understanding of the reasons for the change in auditors
The audit fees the predecessor charged in each of the last two years
The sample sizes the predecessor used for its tests of controls
questions.exp: AU-C 210 requires inquiries about management integrity, disagreements with management, communications with those charged with governance about fraud, noncompliance and internal control matters, and the predecessor's understanding of the reasons for the change. Detailed risk assessments and sample sizes come from a working-paper review after acceptance, not from the required pre-acceptance inquiries.

questions.q: A prospective audit client refuses to permit the successor auditor to communicate with the predecessor auditor. Under AU-C 210, the successor auditor should
choices: inquire about the reasons for the refusal and consider the implications in deciding whether to accept the engagement
accept the engagement but issue a qualified opinion on opening balances
contact the predecessor anyway, because the communication is required by GAAS
decline the engagement, because GAAS prohibits acceptance in this situation
questions.exp: When a prospective client refuses permission, the successor should ask why and weigh the implications for acceptance (AU-C 210). Declining is not automatically required, and contacting the predecessor without permission would breach the predecessor's confidentiality obligations.

questions.q: During acceptance discussions, management states that it will not allow the auditor to send confirmations to any customers or to observe the physical inventory count, which together are material and pervasive to the financial statements. No law or regulation requires the audit. Under AU-C 210, the auditor should
choices: accept the engagement and rely on alternative procedures for both areas
accept the engagement and plan to issue a qualified opinion
accept the engagement and include an emphasis-of-matter paragraph describing the limitation
not accept the limited engagement as an audit engagement
questions.exp: If management imposes a scope limitation before acceptance that the auditor believes would result in a disclaimer of opinion, AU-C 210 says not to accept it as an audit engagement unless law or regulation requires it. A qualified opinion is the trap, but a material and pervasive limitation leads to a disclaimer, not a qualification.

questions.q: Under AU-C 210, which of the following is a precondition for an audit?
choices: The auditor has assessed control risk below the maximum for significant assertions
Management has agreed to record all misstatements the auditor identifies
The entity maintains an internal audit function that reports to those charged with governance
Management acknowledges its responsibility for the design, implementation, and maintenance of internal control relevant to the preparation and fair presentation of the financial statements
questions.exp: The preconditions are an acceptable financial reporting framework and management's agreement that it is responsible for the financial statements, for relevant internal control, and for giving the auditor access and information (AU-C 210). Management is not required to agree in advance to record every misstatement. Uncorrected misstatements are evaluated and listed in the representation letter.

questions.q: Which of the following is required to be included in an audit engagement letter under AU-C 210?
choices: The names and roles of all engagement team members
A statement that, because of the inherent limitations of an audit, there is an unavoidable risk that some material misstatements may not be detected
The planned level of overall materiality for the financial statements
The fee arrangement and billing schedule for the engagement
questions.exp: AU-C 210 requires the letter to cover the objective and scope, the responsibilities of the auditor and of management, the inherent-limitation statement, the framework, and the expected form and content of the report. Fees are commonly included but are not a required element, and disclosing materiality would undermine the audit's effectiveness.

questions.q: An auditor is beginning the fourth consecutive annual audit of a client, and the engagement letter was signed in the first year. Under AU-C 210, the auditor should
choices: obtain a new signed engagement letter, because one is required every year
rely on the original letter without further consideration until the client requests a change
obtain a new engagement letter only if the audit fee changes by more than an insignificant amount
assess whether circumstances require the terms of engagement to be revised and whether management needs to be reminded of the existing terms
questions.exp: For recurring audits, AU-C 210 requires the auditor to assess whether the terms need revision and whether to remind the entity of them. A new letter each year is common practice but is not required. The auditor still cannot simply ignore the terms.

questions.q: Partway through an audit of a nonissuer, the client asks the CPA to change the engagement to a review after the CPA requested permission to correspond with the entity's legal counsel and management refused. Under SSARS, if the CPA agrees to the change, the CPA ordinarily would be
choices: precluded from issuing a review report
permitted to issue a review report as long as the refusal is disclosed in the notes
able to issue a review report with a paragraph emphasizing the limitation
required to refer to the original audit engagement in the review report
questions.exp: Under AR-C 90, if the client prohibited the accountant from corresponding with legal counsel during the audit, the accountant ordinarily would be precluded from issuing a review report. Even when a change is justified, the review report should not refer to the original engagement.

questions.q: Which of the following would most likely be documented in the detailed audit plan rather than in the overall audit strategy?
choices: The reporting deadlines and key dates for communications with those charged with governance
The overall direction and allocation of senior engagement team members to high-risk areas
The nature, timing, and extent of planned further audit procedures at the relevant assertion level
The characteristics of the engagement that define its scope, such as the financial reporting framework
questions.exp: Under AU-C 300, the audit plan sets out the nature, timing, and extent of risk assessment procedures and further procedures at the assertion level. Scope characteristics, reporting objectives and timing, and resource direction belong to the overall audit strategy.

questions.q: Under GAAS, analytical procedures are required to be performed during which phases of a financial statement audit?
choices: Risk assessment, substantive testing, and the overall review near the end of the audit
Risk assessment and the overall review near the end of the audit
The overall review near the end of the audit only
Substantive testing only
questions.exp: Analytical procedures are required as risk assessment procedures (AU-C 315) and in forming an overall conclusion near the end of the audit (AU-C 520). Substantive analytical procedures are optional and are chosen when they are effective and efficient for an assertion.

questions.q: Which of the following is a preliminary engagement activity that AU-C 300 requires at the beginning of the current audit engagement?
choices: Performing tests of operating effectiveness of controls over cash disbursements
Evaluating compliance with relevant ethical requirements, including independence
Obtaining the management representation letter
Sending positive confirmation requests to major customers
questions.exp: AU-C 300 requires preliminary activities on client continuance, on evaluating compliance with ethical requirements including independence, and on establishing the terms of engagement. Confirmations and tests of controls are further audit procedures, and the representation letter is obtained near the report date.

questions.q: An auditor used an external actuary to evaluate a client's pension obligation and is issuing an unmodified opinion. Under AU-C 620, the auditor's report should
choices: refer to the actuary only if the actuary's fee was material to the engagement
not refer to the actuary unless required by law or regulation
name the actuary and state that the auditor relied on the actuary's findings
refer to the actuary to signal a division of responsibility for the pension amounts
questions.exp: AU-C 620 prohibits referring to an auditor's specialist in an unmodified report unless law or regulation requires it, because the auditor takes sole responsibility for the opinion. Specialists are not treated like component auditors, so no division of responsibility is possible.

questions.q: In deciding whether the work of the entity's internal audit function can be used for purposes of the audit, which factor is most important under AU-C 610?
choices: The number of internal auditors relative to the size of the entity
Whether the internal audit function reports administratively to the chief financial officer
The extent to which the function's organizational status and relevant policies and procedures support the objectivity of the internal auditors
Whether the internal auditors hold professional certifications in information systems
questions.exp: AU-C 610 requires the external auditor to evaluate the function's objectivity (organizational status and policies), its competence, and whether it applies a systematic and disciplined approach. Headcount is not a criterion, and administrative reporting to the CFO tends to weaken objectivity rather than support it.

questions.q: A group auditor decides to make reference to the audit of a component auditor in the auditor's report on the group financial statements. The group auditor's report should
choices: state that the group auditor assumes full responsibility for the component auditor's work
name the component auditor even if the component auditor has not given permission
be qualified because part of the financial statements was audited by another auditor
indicate the magnitude of the portion of the group financial statements audited by the component auditor
questions.exp: When reference is made under AU-C 600, the report states that the component was audited by another auditor and shows the magnitude of that portion, such as the percentage of total assets and revenues. Naming the component auditor requires its permission, and making reference is not a modification of the opinion.

questions.q: Which of the following statements is consistent with the engagement team discussion required by AU-C 240 and AU-C 315?
choices: The discussion can be replaced by the documented risk assessment from the prior-year audit
The discussion should emphasize how and where the financial statements might be susceptible to material misstatement due to fraud, setting aside beliefs that management is honest
The discussion should be limited to the engagement partner and the engagement manager
The discussion is required only when the auditor has identified fraud risk factors
questions.exp: Key team members must discuss the susceptibility of the financial statements to material misstatement, including how fraud could be perpetrated and concealed, with professional skepticism and setting aside beliefs about management's integrity. The discussion is required on every audit, not only when risk factors are present.

questions.q: Under SQMS No. 1, who is responsible for evaluating the firm's system of quality management and concluding whether it provides reasonable assurance that its objectives are being achieved, and how often?
choices: The firm's monitoring personnel, only when a deficiency is identified
The engagement quality reviewer on each engagement, at the completion of that engagement
An external peer reviewer, once every three years
The individual or individuals assigned ultimate responsibility and accountability for the system, at least annually
questions.exp: SQMS No. 1 requires the individual or individuals with ultimate responsibility and accountability for the system to evaluate it at least annually and conclude on it. Peer review is a separate AICPA program, not the firm's own required evaluation.

questions.q: Under the AICPA quality management standards, a partner who served as engagement partner on an audit may not be appointed as the engagement quality reviewer for that audit until a cooling-off period of at least how long has passed?
choices: Two years
One year
Three years
Five years
questions.exp: SQMS No. 2 requires the firm's policies to set a cooling-off period of two years before a former engagement partner can serve as engagement quality reviewer on that engagement. Five years is the SEC partner-rotation period, which is a different rule.

questions.q: The engagement partner and the engagement quality reviewer disagree about whether a significant accounting estimate is reasonable. Under the AICPA quality management standards, which of the following is appropriate?
choices: The auditor's report should not be dated until the matter is resolved under the firm's policies for differences of opinion
The engagement quality reviewer's view automatically prevails
The engagement partner may release the report because the engagement partner has final authority
The report may be released if the disagreement is documented in the working papers
questions.exp: Under AU-C 220 and SQMS No. 2, the report cannot be dated until the engagement quality review is complete, which means differences of opinion must be resolved first. Documenting the disagreement does not substitute for resolving it, and neither party's view automatically prevails.

questions.q: An auditor is engaged after year-end and could not observe the client's year-end physical inventory, which is material. The client takes a complete physical count three weeks after year-end, which the auditor observes. Which of the following is most appropriate?
choices: The auditor must disclaim an opinion because the year-end count was not observed
The auditor must issue a qualified opinion but may describe the alternative procedures performed
The auditor may be able to obtain sufficient evidence by observing the later count and testing intervening transactions to roll the quantities back to year-end
The auditor may rely on management's written representation about year-end quantities instead of further procedures
questions.exp: AU-C 501 allows the auditor to attend a count at a date other than year-end and perform procedures on intervening transactions to obtain evidence about changes between the count date and year-end. A modified opinion is needed only if sufficient evidence cannot be obtained, and representations alone are never enough.

questions.q: In a first-year audit, the successor auditor reviews the predecessor auditor's working papers. Which statement is correct under AU-C 510?
choices: The successor may state in its report that its opinion on opening balances is based on the predecessor's working papers
The review may affect the nature, timing, and extent of the successor's procedures on opening balances, but the successor remains responsible for the evidence obtained
The review must be completed before the successor accepts the engagement
The review eliminates the need for any audit procedures on opening balances
questions.exp: Reviewing the predecessor's working papers can provide evidence about opening balances and consistency, but the successor decides what further work is needed and cannot refer to the predecessor's work as a basis for its own opinion. The working-paper review happens after acceptance.

questions.q: Before granting a successor auditor access to its audit working papers, a predecessor auditor ordinarily
choices: requires the former client to waive any claims against the predecessor
obtains written consent from the former client and requests an acknowledgment letter from the successor about the use of the working papers
requires the successor to pay for the predecessor's time at standard billing rates
provides the working papers only after the successor issues its first report
questions.exp: AU-C 510 guidance indicates the predecessor ordinarily obtains a consent letter from the former client and an acknowledgment letter from the successor that limits how the working papers may be used. Access is typically given before the successor completes its first audit so the papers can help with opening balances.

questions.q: During a first-year audit, the successor auditor finds information indicating that the prior-year financial statements reported on by the predecessor auditor may be materially misstated. Under AU-C 510, the successor should
choices: request that management inform the predecessor auditor and arrange a meeting among the three parties to discuss and attempt to resolve the matter
restate the prior-year financial statements in the current-year comparative presentation without further discussion
report the matter directly to the state board of accountancy
withdraw from the engagement immediately
questions.exp: The successor should ask management to inform the predecessor and arrange a meeting among the three parties. If management refuses or the successor is not satisfied with the resolution, the successor considers the implications and may consult legal counsel. Withdrawal is not the automatic first step.

questions.q: In an integrated audit of an issuer with many operating locations, PCAOB AS 2101 directs the auditor to determine the amount of audit attention devoted to individual locations primarily based on
choices: the proportion of consolidated revenue at each location, with every location above 10% fully audited
a rotation plan under which each location is visited at least once every three years
the locations where management prefers the auditor to perform procedures
the risks of material misstatement associated with each location or business unit
questions.exp: AS 2101 requires a risk-based approach for multi-location engagements: the auditor assesses the RMM associated with each location and sets the extent of procedures accordingly. Fixed coverage percentages or rotation schedules do not replace that risk assessment.

questions.q: Under AU-C 260, which of the following should the auditor communicate to those charged with governance regarding the planned scope and timing of the audit?
choices: The detailed audit procedures to be performed on management's estimates
The specific sample sizes and items selected for each significant risk
An overview of the planned scope and timing, including the significant risks identified by the auditor
The exact dates of unannounced cash counts and inventory test counts
questions.exp: AU-C 260 requires an overview of the planned scope and timing, including significant risks. The communication should avoid procedure-level detail, such as sample selections or surprise procedures, because that could make the procedures predictable and less effective.

questions.q: A firm is evaluating whether to accept a new audit client in a highly specialized industry in which the firm has no prior experience. Under SQMS No. 1, the firm's acceptance policies require it to consider
choices: only whether the engagement fee is sufficient to be profitable
only whether the client's management has integrity
whether the firm can complete the engagement before the client's filing deadline, without regard to expertise
whether the firm has the competence, capabilities, time, and resources to perform the engagement in accordance with professional standards
questions.exp: SQMS No. 1 requires acceptance and continuance judgments to consider the nature and circumstances of the engagement, the integrity and ethical values of the client, and the firm's ability to perform it, including competence, capabilities, time, and resources. Integrity alone is not sufficient, and financial priorities should not override quality.

questions.q: Which of the following is required when an accountant is engaged to prepare financial statements for a nonissuer under SSARS (AR-C 70)?
choices: Issuance of a preparation report on each set of financial statements
A determination that the accountant is independent of the entity
Written agreement on the terms of the engagement in an engagement letter signed by the accountant and management or those charged with governance
Performance of analytical procedures and inquiries sufficient for limited assurance
questions.exp: AR-C 70 requires a written engagement letter signed by both parties. Independence is not required and no report is issued, but each page must state that no assurance is provided. Analytical procedures and inquiries for limited assurance belong to a review under AR-C 90.

questions.q: Under GAAS, the extent of supervision of engagement team members depends most directly on
choices: the number of years the firm has audited the client
the complexity of the subject matter and the knowledge, skill, and ability of the team members performing the work
whether the engagement partner holds a CPA license in the client's state
the audit fee negotiated with the client
questions.exp: AU-C 300 indicates that the nature, timing, and extent of direction and supervision vary with the entity's size and complexity, the area of the audit, the assessed RMM, and the capabilities and competence of the team members. Tenure with the client may affect familiarity but is not the driver.

questions.q: Which of the following planning activities applies to an initial audit but not to a recurring audit?
choices: Establishing materiality for the financial statements as a whole
Determining the overall audit strategy and audit plan
Making arrangements to communicate with the predecessor auditor, including about reviewing its working papers
Performing risk assessment procedures to obtain an understanding of the entity
questions.exp: AU-C 300 lists additional initial-audit matters, such as arrangements with the predecessor, procedures on opening balances, and major issues discussed with management at selection. Materiality, risk assessment, and the strategy and plan are required on every audit.

questions.q: During fieldwork, the auditor finds misstatements in accounts payable that are much larger and more frequent than expected, indicating that the assessed risk of material misstatement was too low. Under AU-C 300 and AU-C 315, the auditor should
choices: issue a qualified opinion on accounts payable
request that management correct the misstatements found and make no other changes
revise the risk assessment, overall audit strategy, and audit plan, and modify the planned further audit procedures as necessary
continue performing the procedures in the original audit plan, since planning is complete once fieldwork begins
questions.exp: Planning is a continual, iterative process. When new information contradicts the original risk assessment, the auditor revises the assessment, strategy, and plan and responds with additional or different procedures. Correcting only the misstatements found ignores the likelihood of further misstatement.

questions.q: A predecessor auditor receives a successor auditor's inquiries but decides that, because of threatened litigation with the former client, it will not respond fully. Under AU-C 210, the predecessor should
choices: indicate clearly that its response is limited
refer the successor to the former client's legal counsel for all answers
decline to respond without giving any indication of the reason
provide a full response because GAAS overrides confidentiality
questions.exp: In unusual circumstances, such as impending or threatened litigation, the predecessor may limit its response but should clearly say that the response is limited. The successor then weighs that limited response in deciding whether to accept the engagement.

questions.q: Under PCAOB AS 1301, the auditor of an issuer is required to establish an understanding of the terms of the audit engagement with the audit committee and to
choices: record the understanding in an engagement letter and provide the engagement letter to the audit committee annually
file the engagement letter with the PCAOB before beginning fieldwork
obtain shareholder ratification of the engagement letter each year
obtain the CFO's signature on the engagement letter instead of the audit committee's
questions.exp: AS 1301 requires the auditor to establish the terms with the audit committee, record them in an engagement letter, and provide that letter to the audit committee each year. Shareholder ratification of the auditor is a company governance practice, not a PCAOB requirement.

topics.topic: Ethics, independence and the AICPA Code

questions.q: An audit partner on the engagement for Client Co., a nonissuer, learns that her spouse bought 50 shares of Client Co. stock in a personal brokerage account. The shares are immaterial to the couple's net worth. Under the AICPA Code of Professional Conduct, independence is
choices: not impaired, because the shares are held by the spouse rather than the partner
not impaired, because the investment is immaterial
impaired only if the spouse also holds a key position at Client Co.
impaired, because an immediate family member's direct financial interest is attributed to the covered member regardless of materiality
questions.exp: Under the Code, an immediate family member's financial interests are treated as the covered member's, and any direct financial interest in an attest client impairs independence regardless of materiality. Materiality matters only for indirect financial interests, so the immateriality argument does not help here.

questions.q: A staff accountant assigned to the audit of a nonissuer learns that her older sister, who does not depend on her financially, was just promoted to controller of the client. Under the AICPA Code, independence is
choices: impaired, because an attest engagement team member has a close relative in a key position with the client
impaired only if the staff accountant audits the accounts the sister supervises
not impaired, because a sister is not an immediate family member
not impaired unless the sister also owns shares of the client
questions.exp: Siblings are close relatives. Independence is impaired when an individual on the attest engagement team has a close relative in a key position, such as controller, or with a material financial interest in the client. The immediate-family distinction is the trap, because close relatives are covered by a separate rule.

questions.q: Each of the following individuals at a CPA firm owns 100 shares of a nonissuer audit client, an immaterial amount. Whose ownership impairs the firm's independence under the AICPA Code?
choices: A staff accountant in another office who has no involvement with the client
A tax partner who practices in the same office as the lead attest engagement partner but provides no services to the client
A partner in another office who provides no services to the client
A manager in another office who provided 5 hours of tax services to the client
questions.exp: Covered members include partners in the office where the lead attest engagement partner primarily practices, whether or not they work on the client. Partners and managers in other offices become covered members only if they provide 10 or more hours of nonattest services, and partners in other offices are otherwise limited only to not owning more than 5% of the client.

questions.q: A covered member obtains each of the following loans from a bank that is an attest client, under the bank's normal lending procedures, terms, and requirements. Which loan impairs independence under the AICPA Code?
choices: Credit card balances that are reduced to $10,000 or less by the payment due date
An automobile loan collateralized by the automobile
A new home mortgage on the covered member's primary residence
A loan fully collateralized by a certificate of deposit at the bank
questions.exp: Auto loans collateralized by the vehicle, loans fully collateralized by cash deposits, and credit card balances of $10,000 or less by the due date are permitted loans. A home mortgage is acceptable only if it is grandfathered (obtained before the lender became an attest client or before the member became a covered member). A new mortgage impairs independence.

questions.q: A CPA firm expects to issue its report on Client X's 20X2 financial statements on March 10, 20X3. Fees for the 20X1 audit, rendered and billed in February 20X2, are still unpaid. Under the AICPA Code, the firm's independence is
choices: not impaired, as long as the client signs a promissory note for the unpaid fees before the report is issued
impaired unless the past-due fees are paid before the 20X2 report is issued
not impaired, because fees are an issue only if they are material to the firm
impaired, and paying the fees before the report date cannot cure the impairment
questions.exp: Independence is impaired if fees for professional services rendered more than one year before the current report date remain unpaid when the report is issued, because the unpaid fees act like a loan to the client. Paying them before issuance removes the impairment. Converting them into a note does not, because the fees are still unpaid.

questions.q: A CPA performs several nonattest services for a nonissuer audit client. Which of the following services impairs independence under the AICPA Code?
choices: Approving vendor invoices for payment on the client's behalf
Recording client-approved adjusting journal entries in the general ledger
Recommending improvements to the client's chart of accounts
Preparing the client's federal income tax return for management's review and approval
questions.exp: Authorizing or approving transactions is a management responsibility, which impairs independence under the nonattest services rules. Bookkeeping based on client-approved data, tax preparation, and recommendations are allowed if the general requirements are met, including management making all decisions.

questions.q: A CPA firm provides bookkeeping services to a nonissuer audit client. Under the general requirements for nonattest services in the AICPA Code, which of the following must be true?
choices: The client designates an individual with suitable skill, knowledge, and/or experience to oversee the services
The firm must disclose the bookkeeping services in its audit report
The client must have an audit committee that preapproves the services
The individual overseeing the services must be a CPA or have equivalent credentials
questions.exp: The Code requires the client to designate an individual with suitable skill, knowledge, and/or experience (SKE), who need not be able to perform the service, to oversee it, evaluate its adequacy, make decisions, and accept responsibility. A CPA credential is not required, and audit committee preapproval is an SEC/PCAOB rule for issuers.

questions.q: A CPA firm performs no attest services for a client. Under the AICPA Code, which of the following contingent fee arrangements with that client is prohibited?
choices: A fee for litigation consulting that is fixed by a court
Representing the client in an IRS examination of a previously filed income tax return, with the fee based on the outcome
A consulting fee based on a percentage of cost savings achieved from a new inventory system
Preparing the client's original income tax return, with the fee based on the amount of the refund obtained
questions.exp: Contingent fees are prohibited for preparing an original or amended tax return or claim for refund for any client. Fees fixed by courts and representation in an IRS examination are permitted exceptions, and contingent consulting fees are allowed for clients for whom the firm performs no attest services.

questions.q: A CPA who prepares only the individual income tax return for a client receives a commission from a software vendor for recommending the vendor's budgeting software to that client. Under the AICPA Code, the commission is
choices: prohibited for all clients
prohibited, because the CPA prepares the client's tax return
permitted, provided it is disclosed to the client
permitted only if the commission is less than the tax preparation fee
questions.exp: Commissions are prohibited only for clients for whom the member performs certain attest services, such as audits, reviews, some compilations, and examinations of prospective financial information. For other clients, they are permitted if disclosed to the client. Tax return preparation is not a trigger for the commission prohibition, though it is for contingent fees.

questions.q: An audit partner leaves a CPA firm to become CFO of a nonissuer attest client of the firm. Under the AICPA Code, which of the following conditions is necessary to avoid impairing the firm's independence?
choices: The firm must withdraw from the engagement for one year
The former partner must wait one year before accepting the CFO position
Any amounts due to the former partner are fixed as to amount and payment dates and are not material to the firm
The former partner must sell any retirement interest in the firm, regardless of amount
questions.exp: For nonissuers, the Code allows a former partner to join an attest client in a key position if certain conditions are met. These include fixed, immaterial amounts due from the firm, no continued influence over or participation in the firm's operations, and assessment of the threats and safeguards. The one-year wait is the SEC cooling-off rule for issuers, not an AICPA requirement.

questions.q: An audit manager who worked on the current-year audit of an issuer leaves the firm and is hired as the issuer's controller before that audit is completed. Under SEC independence rules, the audit firm's independence is
choices: impaired, because the manager took a financial reporting oversight role within the one-year cooling-off period
not impaired, because a controller is not a financial reporting oversight role
not impaired, as long as the manager is removed from the engagement team immediately
not impaired, because the cooling-off rule applies only to audit partners
questions.exp: The SEC's one-year cooling-off period applies to members of the audit engagement team, not only partners, who take a financial reporting oversight role such as CEO, CFO, controller, or chief accounting officer. Removing the person from the team does not cure the impairment, and a controller clearly has financial reporting oversight.

questions.q: Under SEC rules applicable to audits of issuers, the lead audit partner and the engagement quality reviewer must rotate off the engagement after serving for
choices: five consecutive years, followed by a five-year time-out
seven consecutive years, followed by a two-year time-out
ten consecutive years, followed by a three-year time-out
three consecutive years, followed by a one-year time-out
questions.exp: The SEC requires the lead and concurring (EQR) partners to rotate after five years, followed by a five-year time-out. The seven-year, two-year-time-out rule applies to other audit partners, which makes it the tempting wrong answer.

questions.q: A PCAOB-registered firm audits an issuer. Which of the following services may the firm provide to the issuer if the audit committee preapproves it?
choices: Fairness opinions and valuation services for an acquisition
Tax compliance services for the company
Bookkeeping services for a subsidiary
Outsourced internal audit services related to internal control over financial reporting
questions.exp: Sarbanes-Oxley and SEC rules prohibit bookkeeping, appraisal or valuation services and fairness opinions, and internal audit outsourcing for issuer audit clients. Most tax compliance services for the company are allowed with audit committee preapproval, although tax services to persons in financial reporting oversight roles and aggressive tax shelters are prohibited.

questions.q: A former client that has not paid outstanding fees asks a CPA to return the original general ledger and source documents it gave the CPA. Under the AICPA Code, the CPA
choices: must give the client copies of the CPA's own audit working papers along with the records
may retain the records indefinitely if the CPA's engagement letter allows it
must return the client-provided records within a reasonable time, even though fees are unpaid
may retain the client-provided records until the outstanding fees are paid
questions.exp: Under the acts discreditable rule, client-provided records must be returned on request (generally within 45 days) even when fees are unpaid. Withholding them is a violation. Member-prepared records and working papers may be treated differently, and working papers belong to the member.

questions.q: Without the client's consent, a CPA discloses confidential client information in each of the following situations. Which disclosure violates the AICPA Code?
choices: Making working papers available to the firm's peer reviewer
Providing the client's financial information to a bank that asked the CPA for it while evaluating a loan application from the client
Responding to an inquiry from the AICPA's professional ethics division
Responding to a validly issued and enforceable subpoena
questions.exp: The confidentiality rule allows disclosure without consent for enforceable subpoenas, peer reviews, and ethics investigations. Giving information to a third-party lender requires the client's specific consent, even if it would help the client obtain the loan.

questions.q: A CPA firm designed and implemented the general ledger system of a nonissuer audit client and now audits the financial statements produced by that system. Under the conceptual framework in the AICPA Code, which threat to independence is most directly created?
choices: Adverse interest threat
Undue influence threat
Advocacy threat
Self-review threat
questions.exp: A self-review threat arises when the firm evaluates results of its own previous services as part of the attest engagement. Advocacy involves promoting the client's interests, and undue influence involves pressure from the client, so neither fits.

questions.q: The current management of a nonissuer attest client files a lawsuit against the CPA firm alleging that the firm's prior-year audit was deficient. Under the AICPA Code, the firm's independence for the current-year audit is
choices: not impaired, because the lawsuit relates to a prior period
impaired, because litigation by present management alleging audit deficiencies creates an adverse interest
not impaired unless the claim is material to the firm
impaired only if the lawsuit seeks punitive damages
questions.exp: The Code treats the commencement of litigation by the client's present management alleging deficiencies in audit work as impairing independence, because the firm and management are now adversaries. The materiality of the claim does not change that result.

questions.q: To thank the engagement partner for completing the audit early, an attest client offers the partner an all-expenses-paid weekend at a resort, valued at about $5,000. No business is involved. Under the AICPA Code, if the partner accepts, independence is
choices: not impaired, as long as the partner reports the gift to the firm
impaired, because the gift is more than clearly insignificant to the recipient
not impaired, because gifts are evaluated only for issuer clients
impaired only if the partner also accepted gifts in the prior year
questions.exp: Accepting a gift from an attest client impairs independence unless the value is clearly insignificant to the recipient. A $5,000 resort weekend unrelated to business is not insignificant, and reporting it internally does not cure the impairment.

questions.q: A partner in the office of the lead attest engagement partner serves on the board of a nonprofit organization that is an attest client. The partner's role is purely honorary: the partner is identified as honorary in all materials, does not vote, and does not participate in management or board decisions. Under the AICPA Code, independence is
choices: impaired, because a covered member may not be associated with an attest client's board in any capacity
not impaired only if the organization's revenues are below a specified threshold
impaired unless the partner resigns before the attest report is issued
not impaired, because the honorary position meets the Code's conditions
questions.exp: The Code allows honorary directorships of not-for-profit attest clients when the position is clearly honorary, the member is identified as honorary, and the member cannot vote or take part in management. Any other board membership would impair independence.

questions.q: The spouse of a senior on the audit engagement team works as a receptionist for the nonissuer audit client and has no financial interest in the client. Under the AICPA Code, independence is
choices: not impaired, because a receptionist is not a key position
not impaired only if the spouse earns less than the senior
impaired, because an immediate family member is employed by the client
impaired unless the senior is removed from the engagement
questions.exp: Employment of an immediate family member impairs independence only if the position is a key position, such as one with primary responsibility for significant accounting functions or the ability to influence the financial statements. A receptionist does not have those responsibilities.

questions.q: On March 1, 20X2, a CPA signs an engagement letter to audit a nonissuer's financial statements for the year ended December 31, 20X1. The CPA owned shares of the client until she sold them on April 10, 20X2, before beginning fieldwork. Under the AICPA Code, independence is
choices: not impaired, because she did not own the shares during fieldwork
impaired only if the shares were material to her net worth
not impaired, because the shares were sold before the report was issued
impaired, because she held a direct financial interest during the period of the professional engagement
questions.exp: The period of professional engagement begins when the member signs the engagement letter or begins the services, whichever is earlier. Holding any direct financial interest after March 1 impairs independence. Selling before fieldwork or before the report is issued does not fix the impairment.

questions.q: A covered member owns 2% of the outstanding shares of a well-diversified mutual fund. The fund holds a small percentage of its assets in shares of the member's attest client. Under the AICPA Code, independence is
choices: impaired unless the member sells the fund shares before the report date
not impaired only if the member also has no other investment in the client's industry
impaired, because owning fund shares is a direct financial interest in the client
not impaired, because the fund's holding is an indirect interest that is not considered material when the member owns 5% or less of a diversified fund
questions.exp: The fund shares are a direct interest in the fund, but the fund's underlying holdings are indirect interests to the member. If the member owns 5% or less of a diversified fund, the underlying investments are not considered material. Only a material indirect interest would impair independence.

questions.q: Under Government Auditing Standards (GAGAS), an auditor plans to prepare an audited entity's financial statements in their entirety from the client-provided trial balance. Which statement is correct?
choices: The service always impairs independence and cannot be performed
The service is a significant threat to independence that the auditor must document and address with safeguards that eliminate or reduce it to an acceptable level
The service creates no threat if management approves the statements
The service may be performed only if the entity's governing body is independent of management
questions.exp: GAGAS treats preparing financial statements in their entirety from a trial balance or underlying records as a significant threat. The auditor must document it and apply safeguards to eliminate it or reduce it to an acceptable level. It does not automatically impair independence, but it is never threat-free either.

questions.q: A CPA firm belongs to an international network of firms that share common branding and quality management policies. Under the AICPA Code, other firms in the network
choices: generally must be independent of the firm's financial statement audit and review clients
must be independent only of the firm's issuer audit clients
need not consider independence, because each is a separate legal entity
must be independent only if they share the firm's exact legal name
questions.exp: The Code's network firm interpretation requires network firms to be independent of the financial statement audit and review clients of the other network firms. Being a separate legal entity does not exempt a firm when there is a shared brand and common quality control.

questions.q: The controller of a manufacturing company is a CPA. The CFO directs her to record revenue for goods that have not shipped. She concludes the entry would cause a material misstatement. Under the AICPA Code's guidance on subordination of judgment, she should next
choices: discuss her concerns with an appropriate higher level of management or those charged with governance
resign immediately without discussing the matter further
record the entry, because the CFO is responsible for the financial statements
report the matter to the state board of accountancy before taking any other step
questions.exp: When a member in business concludes that a supervisor's position would cause a material misstatement, the Code directs the member to take the concern to higher management or those charged with governance and to document it. She may then consider other steps, such as resigning. Recording the entry would subordinate her judgment, and external reporting is not the required first step.

questions.q: A CPA is asked to perform a consulting engagement in an industry in which the CPA has no prior experience. Under the AICPA Code's general standards, the CPA
choices: may accept only if the client waives any claims related to the CPA's inexperience
may accept if the CPA expects to obtain the needed competence through research, consultation, or engaging others before completing the engagement
must decline the engagement, because competence must exist before acceptance
may accept as long as the engagement letter discloses the lack of experience
questions.exp: Under the Code's professional competence standard, a member may accept an engagement when the member can reasonably expect to complete it with professional competence, which can be gained through research or consultation. Prior industry experience is not required, and disclosure in the engagement letter does not substitute for competence.

questions.q: While auditing a nonissuer, a CPA becomes aware of information suggesting that the client may have violated environmental laws that could result in material fines. Under the AICPA Code's interpretation on responding to noncompliance with laws and regulations, the CPA should
choices: ignore the matter, because legal compliance is management's responsibility
discuss the matter with the appropriate level of management and, as appropriate, those charged with governance
report the matter directly to the appropriate regulatory authority in all cases
withdraw from the engagement immediately
questions.exp: The interpretation requires the member to obtain an understanding of the matter and discuss it with management and, where appropriate, those charged with governance. The member then considers further action, such as disclosure where required by law or withdrawal. Automatic external reporting is not required and could breach confidentiality.

questions.q: A CPA firm offers to keep a nonissuer audit client's only copy of its financial data on the firm's servers, acting as the custodian and system of record for the data. Under the AICPA Code, accepting this hosting arrangement
choices: impairs independence only if the firm also prepares the client's tax returns
does not impair independence if the client pays a separate fee for hosting
does not impair independence if the firm encrypts the data
impairs independence, because taking custody of the client's data and records is a management responsibility
questions.exp: The Code's hosting interpretation says that a member who becomes the custodian of client data or records, so that the client relies on the member for its system of record, assumes a management responsibility that impairs independence. Encryption and separate billing do not change who has custody.

questions.q: A nonissuer audit client's engagement letter states that the client will indemnify the CPA firm for any losses resulting from knowing misrepresentations by client management. Under the AICPA Code, this provision
choices: does not impair independence
impairs independence, because it shifts liability to the client
impairs independence only if a claim is actually paid under it
impairs independence unless approved by those charged with governance
questions.exp: The Code's indemnification interpretation states that a client's agreement to indemnify the member for losses from knowing misrepresentations by management does not impair independence. In contrast, a member agreeing to indemnify the client for the client's own losses would create a threat.

questions.q: Under PCAOB Rule 3526, before accepting an initial engagement with an issuer and at least annually thereafter, the registered firm must
choices: obtain written confirmation from the CFO that the firm is independent
describe in writing to the audit committee all relationships between the firm and the company that may reasonably be thought to bear on independence, and discuss their potential effects
obtain shareholder approval of all nonaudit services
file a statement with the SEC listing all nonaudit services provided
questions.exp: Rule 3526 requires written disclosure to the audit committee of relationships that may bear on independence, discussion of their potential effects, and documentation of that discussion, both before the initial engagement and annually. Management cannot confirm the auditor's independence on the auditor's behalf.

topics.topic: Fraud risk and the auditor response (AU-C 240)

questions.q: Under AU-C 240, which of the following must the auditor presume is a fraud risk unless the presumption is rebutted?
choices: Misappropriation of petty cash
Misstatement of related party disclosures
Understatement of accrued liabilities
Improper revenue recognition
questions.exp: AU-C 240 requires the auditor to presume there are risks of material misstatement due to fraud in revenue recognition and to evaluate which types of revenue or assertions give rise to them; the presumption can be rebutted with documentation. Petty cash misappropriation is rarely material and is not a presumed risk.

questions.q: The risk of management override of controls is treated under AU-C 240 as:
choices: A significant risk present in all entities that cannot be rebutted
A risk only for entities with weak internal control
A risk addressed solely by tests of controls
A risk that may be rebutted if management integrity is high
questions.exp: Because management override can occur in any entity, AU-C 240 treats it as a significant risk in all audits and requires specified procedures (journal entries, estimates, unusual transactions) regardless of other assessments. Unlike the revenue presumption, it cannot be rebutted.

questions.q: Which of the following procedures is required in every audit to address the risk of management override of controls?
choices: Confirmation of all bank balances with zero-balance accounts
Retrospective review of management judgments and assumptions in significant accounting estimates reflected in the prior year
Surprise cash counts at year-end
Observation of inventory counts at every location
questions.exp: AU-C 240 requires testing journal entries, reviewing accounting estimates for bias including a retrospective review of prior-year estimates, and evaluating the business rationale of significant unusual transactions. The other procedures may be useful responses but are not universally required.

questions.q: A divisional controller is paid a bonus based on division earnings and faces aggressive targets set by headquarters. This condition is best classified among the fraud risk factors as:
choices: An incentive or pressure
An attitude
An opportunity
A rationalization
questions.exp: Compensation tied to aggressive targets creates an incentive or pressure to commit fraudulent financial reporting. Opportunity relates to circumstances such as weak controls, and attitude/rationalization relates to a mindset that justifies the act.

questions.q: During the engagement team discussion required by AU-C 240, the team should emphasize:
choices: How and where the entity's financial statements might be susceptible to material misstatement due to fraud, setting aside beliefs about management's honesty
The prior-year conclusion that management has high integrity, which allows reduced skepticism
Which team members will be assigned to test cash
The client's planned dividend policy
questions.exp: The brainstorming discussion focuses on how fraud could occur and be concealed, and requires members to set aside any belief that management is honest. Relying on prior beliefs about integrity undermines professional skepticism.

questions.q: An auditor discovers that a warehouse clerk stole inventory worth an immaterial amount. Under AU-C 240, the auditor should:
choices: Report the matter directly to law enforcement
Bring the matter to the attention of an appropriate level of management on a timely basis
Withdraw from the engagement immediately
Ignore the matter because it is immaterial
questions.exp: When the auditor has evidence that fraud may exist, AU-C 240 requires communicating it to an appropriate level of management, even if inconsequential. Fraud involving senior management or causing material misstatement goes to those charged with governance; external reporting is generally not the auditor's duty absent legal requirements.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the inherent limitation the auditor faces with respect to fraud detection?
choices: The risk of not detecting a material misstatement due to fraud is higher than for error because fraud may involve collusion, forgery, and concealment
Auditors are responsible for detecting all frauds regardless of materiality
The auditor is not required to consider fraud in a financial statement audit
Fraud resulting from error is harder to detect than fraud resulting from intentional acts
questions.exp: AU-C 240 explains that fraud is harder to detect than error because it can involve sophisticated concealment, collusion, and management override. Error is by definition unintentional, and the auditor's responsibility is reasonable assurance regarding material misstatement.

questions.q: An auditor identifies a misstatement due to fraud that is not material and involves a mid-level purchasing manager. Which is the most appropriate response?
choices: Discontinue the audit because management representations are now unreliable
Reevaluate the assessment of fraud risk and consider the implications for other aspects of the audit, including the reliability of representations
Conclude that the matter has no implications beyond the specific item
Communicate only in the auditor's report
questions.exp: AU-C 240 requires the auditor to consider whether an identified misstatement may indicate fraud and its implications, since fraud is unlikely to be an isolated occurrence; the auditor reevaluates risks and the reliability of representations. Immaterial fraud does not automatically require withdrawal.

questions.q: Which of the following responses to an assessed fraud risk at the overall financial statement level best incorporates unpredictability?
choices: Performing procedures at locations or on accounts not normally tested, without advance notice to the entity
Using larger samples drawn from the same population tested last year
Performing the same procedures as the prior year so results are comparable
Reducing reliance on substantive procedures
questions.exp: AU-C 240 requires incorporating an element of unpredictability, such as testing locations or balances not normally examined or changing timing. Repeating prior-year procedures is predictable, and merely increasing the sample size in the same area adds little unpredictability.

questions.q: When selecting journal entries to test for management override, the auditor should give particular attention to entries that:
choices: Relate to cash receipts that have been confirmed
Were reviewed by the external auditor in the prior year
Are made at the end of the reporting period, posted by individuals who do not usually make entries, or contain round numbers
Are system-generated and recurring each month
questions.exp: AU-C 240 directs the auditor to focus on entries with fraud-risk characteristics, such as period-end entries, unusual preparers, unrelated or seldom-used accounts, and round numbers. Routine system-generated entries are generally lower risk, though not ignored.

questions.q: An auditor rebuts the presumption that revenue recognition is a fraud risk for a client with a single, simple revenue stream of lease rentals. What is required?
choices: The auditor must still treat revenue as a significant risk
The auditor must obtain written approval from those charged with governance
No documentation is required if the risk is rebutted
The auditor must document the reasons supporting the conclusion that the presumption does not apply
questions.exp: AU-C 240 permits rebutting the revenue presumption in limited circumstances but requires documentation of the reasons. Rebuttal means the auditor does not treat it as a fraud risk; approval by governance is not required.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of misappropriation of assets rather than fraudulent financial reporting?
choices: Recording fictitious sales near year-end to meet analyst expectations
Intentionally omitting disclosure of a guarantee
Deliberately understating the allowance for credit losses
Lapping of customer payments to conceal theft of cash receipts
questions.exp: Lapping conceals theft of cash, so it is misappropriation of assets. Fictitious sales, omitted disclosures, and manipulated estimates are intentional misstatements of the financial statements, which is fraudulent financial reporting.

questions.q: An auditor identifies a significant unusual transaction outside the normal course of business: a sale of land to an entity whose ownership is unclear, recorded on the last day of the year at a large gain. The auditor should primarily:
choices: Limit work to vouching the cash receipt
Accept the transaction because it was approved by the CFO
Evaluate whether the business rationale suggests the transaction may have been entered into to engage in fraudulent financial reporting or conceal misappropriation
Treat the transaction as a subsequent event
questions.exp: AU-C 240 requires evaluating whether the business rationale (or lack of it) of significant unusual transactions suggests fraud. CFO approval alone does not address override risk, and the transaction occurred within the period.

questions.q: Which of the following inquiries is required by AU-C 240 during risk assessment?
choices: Inquiry of the predecessor auditor about client fees
Inquiry of the entity's external legal counsel about fraud
Inquiry of management and others within the entity, including internal audit if applicable and those charged with governance, about knowledge of fraud or suspected fraud
Inquiry of all employees through a written survey
questions.exp: AU-C 240 requires inquiries of management, appropriate others, internal audit, and those charged with governance about fraud risks and known or suspected fraud. Legal counsel and surveys of all employees are not required by the standard.

questions.q: An auditor concludes that the financial statements are materially misstated due to fraud involving the CEO and that the CEO dominates the board. Which is most appropriate?
choices: Expand sample sizes and continue without communication
Issue an unmodified opinion with an emphasis-of-matter paragraph
Consider withdrawing from the engagement where permitted and obtain legal advice, in addition to required communications
Report the fraud to the SEC before discussing with anyone at the entity
questions.exp: AU-C 240 indicates that when fraud raises questions about the auditor's ability to continue, the auditor considers professional and legal responsibilities, including possible withdrawal and legal advice. An emphasis-of-matter paragraph cannot cure a material misstatement.

questions.q: In which situation is the auditor most likely to have a duty to disclose fraud to parties outside the entity?
choices: In response to a subpoena or to a successor auditor's inquiries, with client permission where required
When the fraud involves only immaterial misappropriation
When the auditor believes the board has acted appropriately
When the client asks the auditor to keep the matter confidential
questions.exp: AU-C 240 notes the auditor's ethical duty of confidentiality generally precludes external reporting, but disclosure may be appropriate under legal requirements such as a subpoena, to successor auditors (with consent), or as required by law or regulation. Immateriality does not create an outside reporting duty.

questions.q: Which of the following is an opportunity risk factor for fraudulent financial reporting?
choices: Management's history of violating securities laws
Management's excessive interest in maintaining the stock price
Threats of bankruptcy
Significant related-party transactions not in the ordinary course of business with unaudited related entities
questions.exp: Complex or unusual related-party transactions provide an opportunity to misstate. Interest in the stock price and bankruptcy threats are incentives/pressures, and a history of violations reflects attitude/rationalization.

questions.q: An auditor is evaluating accounting estimates for possible management bias. Which observation is most indicative of bias?
choices: The client uses a specialist for its pension valuation
Estimates changed due to new information that became available
Each estimate is individually within a reasonable range, but all fall at the end of the range that increases earnings
Each estimate is individually reasonable, and estimates are evenly distributed around point estimates
questions.exp: AU-C 240 and AU-C 540 note that individually reasonable estimates that consistently favor one direction may collectively indicate management bias. Changes due to new information or use of specialists are not themselves indicators of bias.

questions.q: An auditor observes that physical inventory counts at the main warehouse are performed with the auditor present but that management requested no auditor attendance at a satellite location. Which response is most appropriate?
choices: Treat the request as a possible fraud risk factor and consider attending or performing unannounced counts at the satellite location
Accept management's request because the satellite is smaller
Disclaim an opinion immediately
Rely on the main warehouse count to cover all locations
questions.exp: Management limiting auditor access to particular locations can signal fraud risk; the auditor responds with unpredictable procedures such as surprise counts at that location. A disclaimer is premature until the auditor determines whether evidence can be obtained.

questions.q: Which of the following is required documentation under AU-C 240?
choices: A copy of the client's code of conduct
A list of every employee interviewed during the audit
The significant decisions reached during the engagement team discussion, the identified and assessed fraud risks, and the auditor's responses
The fee arrangements with the client
questions.exp: AU-C 240 requires documenting the team discussion and significant decisions, identified and assessed risks of material misstatement due to fraud, responses, results of procedures, and communications. A list of every employee interviewed and fee arrangements are not required by AU-C 240.

questions.q: Which statement best describes the auditor's responsibility for detecting fraud under AU-C 240?
choices: To guarantee that no fraud has occurred
To prevent fraud through recommendations on internal control
To detect all misappropriation of assets regardless of amount
To obtain reasonable assurance that the financial statements as a whole are free from material misstatement, whether due to fraud or error
questions.exp: The auditor's objective is reasonable assurance about material misstatement whether caused by fraud or error; prevention and detection are primarily the responsibility of management and those charged with governance. No audit can guarantee absence of fraud.

questions.q: An auditor learns that an employee anonymous hotline complaint alleges that sales personnel are entering into side agreements granting customers unlimited return rights. Which procedure best responds?
choices: Review the minutes of the compensation committee only
Increase the sample of cash disbursements tested
Confirm with customers the terms of sales, including the absence of side agreements and return rights
Recompute depreciation expense
questions.exp: Confirming contract terms directly with customers, including side agreements, is a recommended response in AU-C 240 to revenue fraud risks. Disbursements and depreciation are unrelated to the alleged revenue manipulation.

questions.q: Under PCAOB AS 2401 for an issuer audit, if the auditor determines there is evidence that fraud may exist involving senior management, the auditor should communicate directly to:
choices: Only the CFO
The audit committee
The PCAOB inspections staff
The SEC within one business day
questions.exp: AS 2401 requires fraud involving senior management, or fraud causing material misstatement, to be reported directly to the audit committee. Direct reporting to the SEC arises only under specific Section 10A procedures when the board fails to act appropriately.

questions.q: An auditor's analytical procedures performed near the end of the audit reveal that revenue recognized in the last week of the year is unusually high relative to prior weeks. Under AU-C 240, the auditor should:
choices: Conclude no further action is needed because the overall review is not required to detect fraud
Evaluate whether the result indicates a previously unrecognized risk of material misstatement due to fraud
Reduce materiality for revenue
Defer consideration to the next audit
questions.exp: AU-C 240 requires the auditor to evaluate whether analytical procedures performed near the end of the audit indicate a previously unrecognized risk of material misstatement due to fraud. Deferring or ignoring the unusual trend would fail that requirement.

questions.q: Which of the following is the most likely reason the auditor would test the reconciliation of the general ledger to the trial balance used to prepare the financial statements?
choices: To satisfy the going-concern evaluation
To determine materiality
To evaluate the work of internal audit
To determine that entries and adjustments made in preparing the financial statements, including post-closing entries, are captured for testing
questions.exp: AU-C 240 requires testing entries made in preparing the financial statements, which may bypass the general ledger; reconciling the ledger to the statements helps identify top-side and post-closing adjustments. The reconciliation is unrelated to materiality or going concern.

questions.q: An auditor finds that several shipping documents supporting year-end sales appear altered. The auditor is not trained to authenticate documents. Which is most appropriate?
choices: Investigate further, possibly including confirmation with third parties or use of a specialist to assess authenticity
Remove the sales from the population and continue sampling
Issue a disclaimer of opinion immediately
Accept the documents as genuine because auditors are not expected to authenticate documents
questions.exp: Although auditors are not trained as document authentication experts, AU-C 240 and AU-C 500 require further investigation when conditions indicate a document may not be authentic, such as confirmation or using a specialist. Simply accepting suspicious documents violates professional skepticism.

questions.q: Which of the following is most likely a fraud risk factor relating to attitudes/rationalizations?
choices: Management's practice of committing to analysts to achieve aggressive forecasts and a strained relationship with the current auditor
High dependence on debt financing with restrictive covenants
Rapid growth relative to the industry
Inadequate segregation of duties in the cash function
questions.exp: AU-C 240 lists aggressive commitments to analysts and a strained relationship with the auditor as attitude/rationalization factors. Weak segregation is an opportunity, and rapid growth and debt covenants are pressures.

questions.q: An auditor concludes, after performing procedures, that a material misstatement due to fraud exists but management refuses to correct it. What opinion is appropriate, assuming the effect is material but not pervasive?
choices: Adverse opinion
Qualified opinion
Disclaimer of opinion
Unmodified with an other-matter paragraph
questions.exp: An uncorrected material misstatement that is material but not pervasive results in a qualified opinion under AU-C 705, regardless of whether it stems from fraud or error. An adverse opinion is used when the misstatement is pervasive, and a disclaimer relates to inability to obtain evidence.

questions.q: Which is the most appropriate response to an assessed fraud risk related to inventory quantities at multiple locations?
choices: Observe counts at all locations on the same date or perform counts at selected locations on an unannounced basis
Request a representation that inventory exists
Perform analytical procedures on gross margin only
Rely on management's perpetual records without observation
questions.exp: AU-C 240 suggests simultaneous or unannounced counts as responses to inventory fraud risk, preventing the transfer of goods between locations. Analytics and representations alone do not adequately address the risk of fictitious quantities.

questions.q: An auditor assesses a fraud risk related to the allowance for credit losses at the assertion level. Which response is most appropriately tailored to that risk?
choices: Increase overall materiality to reduce testing
Rely primarily on inquiry of the credit manager
Obtain more reliable and relevant evidence, such as independently evaluating subsequent collections and testing the data and assumptions underlying the estimate
Perform the same procedures used for low-risk accounts at an interim date
questions.exp: AU-C 240 requires responses to assertion-level fraud risks that change the nature, timing, or extent of procedures, such as obtaining more reliable evidence and testing assumptions. Inquiry alone is weak evidence, and interim-only procedures may be less effective for a period-end estimate.
