questions.q: Under AU-C 570 for a nonissuer reporting under U.S. GAAP, over what period does the auditor evaluate whether substantial doubt exists about the entity's ability to continue as a going concern?
choices: One year after the balance sheet date
A reasonable period not to exceed one year beyond the balance sheet date
One year after the date the financial statements are issued or available to be issued
Eighteen months after the report date
questions.exp: When the applicable framework is U.S. GAAP (ASC 205-40), the look-forward period is one year after the financial statements are issued or available to be issued, and AU-C 570 aligns with the framework's period. A period of a reasonable time not exceeding one year beyond the balance sheet date is the PCAOB AS 2415 period.

questions.q: An auditor identifies conditions raising substantial doubt but concludes management's plans alleviate that doubt. Management adequately discloses the conditions and plans. Under AU-C 570, the auditor's report on the nonissuer should:
choices: Include an adverse opinion
Include a qualified opinion
Not be required to include a going concern section, although the auditor may include an emphasis-of-matter paragraph
Include a separate section titled 'Substantial Doubt About the Entity's Ability to Continue as a Going Concern'
questions.exp: When substantial doubt is alleviated by management's plans, AU-C 570 requires evaluating the adequacy of disclosure but does not require a going concern section; an emphasis-of-matter paragraph is optional. The separate section is required only when substantial doubt remains.

questions.q: Which of the following conditions, considered alone, would most likely raise substantial doubt about an entity's ability to continue as a going concern?
choices: The entity's decision to discontinue a profitable product line to focus on another
A significant increase in the allowance for credit losses due to a new accounting standard
Default on a loan agreement, with the lender having the right to accelerate the debt, and denial of credit by key suppliers
The resignation of the entity's controller
questions.exp: Loan default with acceleration rights and loss of trade credit are classic indicators of liquidity problems listed in AU-C 570. An accounting change, a strategic product decision, or a controller's resignation do not by themselves indicate inability to meet obligations.

questions.q: When evaluating management's plans to mitigate going concern conditions, the auditor primarily considers whether:
choices: The plans eliminate all losses in the next year
The plans have been approved by the entity's lenders
The plans were prepared by an outside consultant
It is probable that the plans will be effectively implemented and, if so, that they will mitigate the conditions
questions.exp: AU-C 570 and ASC 205-40 require evaluating whether it is probable that management's plans will be effectively implemented and will mitigate the relevant conditions. Lender approval or consultant preparation may be evidence but are not the standard, and eliminating all losses is not required.

questions.q: Management's plan to alleviate substantial doubt depends on continued financial support from the entity's majority owner. Which evidence is most important for the auditor to obtain?
choices: An oral statement from the CFO that the owner has always provided support
A projection showing the entity will be profitable without support
Evidence of the owner's intent and ability to provide the support, such as a written agreement and the owner's financial capacity
The owner's résumé
questions.exp: AU-C 570 indicates that when plans rely on support from third parties or owners, the auditor evaluates their intent and ability, often through written evidence and the supporter's financial capacity. An oral representation from management is insufficient on its own.

questions.q: An auditor concludes that substantial doubt exists and management's disclosure of the matter is inadequate. The effect is material but not pervasive. The auditor should express:
choices: A disclaimer of opinion
An unmodified opinion with a going concern section
A qualified opinion
An unmodified opinion with an other-matter paragraph
questions.exp: Under AU-C 570 and AU-C 705, inadequate going concern disclosure is a misstatement resulting in a qualified or adverse opinion depending on pervasiveness. A going concern section accompanies an unmodified opinion only when disclosure is adequate.

questions.q: Management of a nonissuer prepared financial statements on the going concern basis, but the auditor concludes liquidation is imminent and the going concern basis is inappropriate. The auditor should:
choices: Issue an unmodified opinion with a going concern section
Express an adverse opinion
Issue a disclaimer of opinion
Issue a qualified opinion
questions.exp: AU-C 570 requires an adverse opinion when the financial statements are prepared using the going concern basis but, in the auditor's judgment, that basis is inappropriate. A going concern section is used when the basis is appropriate but substantial doubt exists.

questions.q: A nonissuer appropriately adopts the liquidation basis of accounting because liquidation is imminent. How should the auditor report, assuming the statements are fairly presented on that basis?
choices: Qualified opinion
Disclaimer because the future is uncertain
Unmodified opinion, and the auditor may include an emphasis-of-matter paragraph about the liquidation basis
Adverse opinion because the going concern basis was not used
questions.exp: When the liquidation basis is appropriate and properly applied, the opinion is unmodified, and an emphasis-of-matter paragraph is generally appropriate to draw attention to the basis. Adverse opinions are reserved for inappropriate use of the going concern basis.

questions.q: Which statement is accurate about wording in the going concern section of an auditor's report under AU-C 570?
choices: The report must name the lenders whose actions caused the doubt
The report may state 'if the company continues to suffer losses, there may be substantial doubt'
The report must use the terms 'substantial doubt' and 'going concern' and must not use conditional language about the conclusion
The report should state the probability that the entity will fail
questions.exp: AU-C 570 requires the terms 'substantial doubt' and 'going concern' and prohibits conditional language that expresses the conclusion tentatively. The report does not quantify probability of failure or name specific lenders.

questions.q: Management refuses to perform an evaluation of the entity's ability to continue as a going concern as required by the applicable framework. The auditor should:
choices: Perform the evaluation on management's behalf and issue an unmodified opinion
Consider the implications for the auditor's report, as this may constitute a scope limitation or misstatement
Ignore the refusal because the auditor makes its own evaluation
Report the refusal to the state board of accountancy
questions.exp: AU-C 570 indicates that management's unwillingness to make or extend its evaluation may have implications for the report, such as a scope limitation. The auditor's own evaluation does not substitute for management's required assessment.

questions.q: When events or conditions raising substantial doubt are identified, which of the following is a required additional procedure under AU-C 570?
choices: Obtaining a legal letter from every vendor
Requesting written representations from management regarding its plans and their feasibility
Confirming all receivables with customers
Reperforming the prior-year audit
questions.exp: AU-C 570 requires additional procedures including evaluating management's plans and requesting written representations about the plans and the probability of their implementation. The other procedures are not specifically required.

questions.q: Management's plans rely on a cash flow forecast projecting significant sales growth. Which procedure is most appropriate?
choices: Compare the forecast to the budget prepared by the same people
Accept the forecast because management is responsible for it
Evaluate the reliability of the underlying data and whether there is adequate support for the significant assumptions
Recompute only the mathematical accuracy of the forecast
questions.exp: When prospective financial information is significant to management's plans, AU-C 570 requires evaluating the reliability of the underlying data and support for significant assumptions. Mathematical accuracy alone does not address whether the projected growth is reasonable.

questions.q: In an issuer audit under PCAOB AS 2415, the period the auditor considers when evaluating going concern is:
choices: Two years beyond the balance sheet date
One year after the date the financial statements are issued
A reasonable period of time, not to exceed one year beyond the date of the financial statements being audited
The operating cycle of the entity
questions.exp: AS 2415 uses a reasonable period not exceeding one year beyond the date of the financial statements being audited. The 'issued or available to be issued' period derives from U.S. GAAP and AU-C 570; the auditor must still consider the framework's disclosure requirements.

questions.q: A nonissuer's prior-year audit report included a going concern section. In the current year, substantial doubt no longer exists. The current comparative report should:
choices: Repeat the prior-year going concern section
Include an adverse opinion on the prior year
Include a qualified opinion on the current year
Not repeat the going concern section
questions.exp: If substantial doubt existed in the prior period but has been removed in the current period, AU-C 570 indicates that the going concern section included in the prior report should not be repeated. No modification is needed for either year.

questions.q: Which of the following is required to be communicated to those charged with governance under AU-C 570 when the auditor identifies events or conditions raising substantial doubt?
choices: The auditor's fee for the additional work
Only the matters that were not resolved by year-end
Whether the events or conditions constitute substantial doubt, the effect on the report, and the adequacy of related disclosures
The names of the employees who prepared the cash flow forecast
questions.exp: AU-C 570 requires communicating whether events or conditions constitute substantial doubt, whether management's plans alleviate it, the adequacy of disclosures, and the implications for the report. Fees and specific employee names are not part of this communication.

questions.q: The absence of reference to substantial doubt in an auditor's report should be viewed as:
choices: A conclusion that no conditions exist that require disclosure
Not a guarantee of the entity's ability to continue as a going concern
A guarantee that the entity will continue as a going concern for one year
Evidence that management's plans are probable of implementation
questions.exp: AU-C 570 states the auditor cannot predict future events, so the absence of a going concern reference does not guarantee continuation. The auditor's evaluation is based on information available at the report date.

questions.q: A nonissuer's financial statements are being audited, and the auditor is concerned about going concern but management has not yet approved the financial statements several months after year-end. How might this delay affect the evaluation?
choices: The auditor should consider the reasons for the delay, which may relate to going concern, and evaluate events through the later date
The delay requires an adverse opinion
The auditor should date the report as of the balance sheet date
The delay has no effect because the look-forward period is fixed from the balance sheet date
questions.exp: AU-C 570 notes that a significant delay in approval may relate to going concern issues and requires the auditor to inquire into the reasons; because the GAAP period runs from the issuance date, the look-forward window also shifts. The report cannot be dated before the auditor obtains sufficient evidence.

questions.q: Which of the following management plans would the auditor most likely view as least effective in mitigating substantial doubt?
choices: A signed commitment from a bank to refinance debt maturing within the year
A plan to sell specialized equipment that is pledged as collateral and restricted from sale under a loan covenant
A plan to sell nonessential assets for which a binding sales agreement exists
A plan to reduce discretionary expenditures that management controls
questions.exp: AU-C 570 directs the auditor to consider restrictions on disposal of assets, such as covenants and liens, when evaluating plans to sell assets; a restricted, pledged asset sale is unlikely to be effectively implemented. Committed financing, binding sale agreements, and controllable cost reductions are more likely to mitigate the conditions.

questions.q: An auditor's going concern evaluation identifies that the entity has a recurring negative operating cash flow but has just closed a new equity raise sufficient to fund operations for 18 months. Management discloses the conditions and the raise. Which conclusion is most appropriate?
choices: Substantial doubt is alleviated, and the auditor evaluates whether disclosures are adequate
The auditor must disclaim because the future is uncertain
An adverse opinion is required
Substantial doubt exists and cannot be alleviated by an equity raise
questions.exp: Completed financing that funds operations beyond the look-forward period is strong evidence alleviating substantial doubt, though disclosure of the conditions and plans is still evaluated under ASC 205-40 and AU-C 570. Uncertainty about the future alone is not a reason to disclaim.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of an event or condition that, under AU-C 570, relates to operating matters rather than financial matters?
choices: Inability to pay creditors on due dates
Arrears in dividends
Loss of a major market, key customers, or principal suppliers
Negative working capital
questions.exp: AU-C 570 lists loss of key markets, customers, or suppliers among operating indicators. Negative working capital, inability to pay creditors, and dividend arrears are financial indicators.

questions.q: An auditor's evaluation of going concern under AU-C 570 is primarily based on:
choices: Inquiry of the entity's legal counsel
A separate set of procedures designed solely to detect going concern issues
Audit procedures performed throughout the audit, considered in the aggregate, plus additional procedures when conditions are identified
The client's credit rating alone
questions.exp: AU-C 570 indicates that the auditor considers whether conditions exist based on procedures performed in planning, gathering evidence, and completing the audit, and performs additional procedures when conditions are identified. No separate set of procedures solely for going concern is required at the outset.

questions.q: A nonissuer auditor concludes substantial doubt exists and disclosures are adequate, but management refuses to provide the requested written representations regarding its plans. The auditor should most likely:
choices: Withdraw immediately without considering the report
Consider the refusal a scope limitation and evaluate the effect on the opinion, which may lead to a disclaimer
Issue an unmodified opinion with a going concern section, ignoring the refusal
Issue an adverse opinion because of the misstatement
questions.exp: Failure to provide required written representations is a scope limitation under AU-C 580, and AU-C 570 requires the auditor to consider its effect, which can result in a disclaimer. An adverse opinion addresses misstatements, not missing evidence.

questions.q: Under PCAOB AS 2415, when the auditor concludes there is substantial doubt about an issuer's ability to continue as a going concern, the auditor's report should include:
choices: An adverse opinion
An explanatory paragraph that includes the phrase 'substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern'
A key audit matter section
A qualified opinion
questions.exp: AS 2415 requires an explanatory paragraph using that phrase when substantial doubt remains, and the opinion is unmodified if disclosure is adequate. Key audit matters are an AU-C 701 concept, and a qualified opinion would arise only from inadequate disclosure.

questions.q: Which statement about the auditor's responsibility for going concern in an audit of a nonissuer is most accurate?
choices: The auditor's responsibility is limited to reviewing management's disclosures
The auditor has no responsibility if management's evaluation concludes there is no substantial doubt
The auditor is responsible for obtaining sufficient appropriate evidence about, and concluding on, management's use of the going concern basis and whether substantial doubt exists
The auditor is responsible for predicting whether the entity will fail
questions.exp: AU-C 570 makes the auditor responsible for evaluating management's use of the going concern basis and concluding whether substantial doubt exists, even when management concludes no doubt exists. The auditor does not predict future events.

questions.q: An auditor determines during an audit that an entity's major lender has waived a covenant violation only through 30 days after year-end, and the debt would otherwise be callable. Which effect is most likely?
choices: The waiver is irrelevant because it was granted after year-end
The auditor must issue an adverse opinion
The short waiver is a condition the auditor considers in the going concern evaluation and may affect classification of the debt
The waiver eliminates any going concern concern
questions.exp: A short-term waiver leaves the debt callable within the look-forward period, which is relevant to both going concern and debt classification. Information after year-end is relevant to the evaluation, so it cannot be ignored.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes when the auditor considers management's plans under AU-C 570?
choices: Only after concluding that events or conditions, considered in the aggregate, raise substantial doubt before consideration of management's plans
Only after the auditor's report has been issued
Before identifying any conditions, as part of engagement acceptance
Only if the client is an issuer
questions.exp: ASC 205-40 and AU-C 570 use a two-step approach: first determine whether conditions raise substantial doubt, then evaluate whether management's plans alleviate it. Plans are not evaluated before conditions are identified.

questions.q: An auditor concludes that substantial doubt exists. The auditor also determines that the matter is so significant that the effects of multiple uncertainties on the financial statements cannot be evaluated. Under AU-C 570, the auditor may:
choices: In rare circumstances involving multiple uncertainties, consider expressing a disclaimer of opinion
Issue a qualified opinion
Omit the going concern section
Issue an adverse opinion
questions.exp: AU-C 570 indicates that in rare cases involving multiple material uncertainties significant to the financial statements, the auditor may disclaim rather than include a going concern section. An adverse opinion is not appropriate for uncertainties that are adequately disclosed.

questions.q: An auditor of a nonissuer included a going concern section in the auditor's report. Which statement about the auditor's opinion is accurate?
choices: The opinion is not modified with respect to the matter, assuming adequate disclosure
The opinion is adverse
The opinion is qualified for the uncertainty
The section replaces the Basis for Opinion section
questions.exp: When disclosure is adequate, the going concern section accompanies an unmodified opinion and states the opinion is not modified with respect to the matter (AU-C 570). It is presented in addition to, not in place of, the Basis for Opinion section.

questions.q: Under AU-C 570, which of the following must the auditor evaluate even when the auditor concludes that no substantial doubt exists?
choices: Whether management's plans have been approved by the lenders
Whether the applicable financial reporting framework requires disclosures about events or conditions identified, and whether those disclosures are adequate
Whether a going concern section must nonetheless be included in the report
Whether the entity has obtained a going concern insurance policy
questions.exp: Even when substantial doubt is not identified, or is alleviated, the auditor considers the framework's disclosure requirements about relevant conditions (AU-C 570). No going concern section is required when there is no substantial doubt.

questions.q: Which of the following procedures is most likely to identify conditions that indicate substantial doubt about going concern?
choices: Observation of the physical inventory count
Recomputation of depreciation expense
Tests of controls over payroll authorization
Review of compliance with the terms of debt and loan agreements
questions.exp: AU-C 570 lists reviewing compliance with debt and loan agreements among procedures that may identify going concern conditions, such as covenant violations that permit acceleration. Payroll controls, inventory counts, and depreciation recalculation are rarely informative about liquidity.

topics.topic: Internal control and the COSO framework

questions.q: A company's board of directors includes a majority of independent members who meet regularly without management to oversee financial reporting, and the company enforces a written code of conduct. Under the COSO 2013 Internal Control-Integrated Framework, these practices relate most directly to which component?
choices: Control environment
Risk assessment
Monitoring activities
Control activities
questions.exp: COSO's control environment principles include commitment to integrity and ethical values and board independence and oversight of internal control. Monitoring is about evaluating whether components are functioning, not about board structure itself.

questions.q: When identifying risks to its financial reporting objectives, management of a public company specifically evaluates incentives and pressures, opportunities, and attitudes that could lead to fraudulent reporting. Under COSO 2013, this activity is part of which component?
choices: Risk assessment
Control activities
Information and communication
Control environment
questions.exp: COSO's risk assessment component includes Principle 8, which requires the organization to consider the potential for fraud when assessing risks to achieving objectives. The control environment sets the tone but is not where fraud risks are identified and analyzed.

questions.q: A company's internal audit department periodically evaluates whether key controls over revenue are operating as designed and reports deficiencies to the audit committee and senior management. Under COSO 2013, this function is part of which component?
choices: Monitoring activities
Risk assessment
Information and communication
Control activities
questions.exp: Separate evaluations, such as internal audit reviews, and the communication of deficiencies to those responsible for corrective action are monitoring activities (COSO Principles 16 and 17). The controls being tested are control activities, but evaluating them is monitoring.

questions.q: A company maintains an anonymous whistleblower hotline that lets employees report suspected improprieties directly to the audit committee, bypassing normal reporting lines. Under COSO 2013, the hotline is most directly an element of which component?
choices: Risk assessment
Control activities
Monitoring activities
Information and communication
questions.exp: COSO Principle 14 (internal communication) specifically mentions separate communication lines, such as whistleblower hotlines, as a way to allow anonymous or confidential communication when normal channels are ineffective. Many candidates choose control environment or monitoring, but COSO places it under information and communication.

questions.q: A company restricts access to its production programs and data so that only authorized IT personnel can make changes. Under COSO 2013, this type of control is classified within which component?
choices: Control activities
Risk assessment
Control environment
Monitoring activities
questions.exp: COSO Principle 11 requires the organization to select and develop general control activities over technology, which include security and access controls. These are control activities, even though they relate to the IT environment.

questions.q: Under the COSO 2013 framework, an effective system of internal control requires that
choices: no deficiencies of any kind exist in any component
the organization has an internal audit function that reports directly to the board
each of the five components and relevant principles is present and functioning, and the components operate together in an integrated manner
all 17 principles are documented in written policies approved by the board
questions.exp: COSO requires each component and relevant principle to be present and functioning, and the five components to operate together, with no major deficiency. Minor deficiencies may exist in an effective system, and COSO does not require an internal audit function or written documentation of every principle.

questions.q: A receiving clerk and an accounts payable clerk agree to process invoices from a fictitious vendor, with the receiving clerk preparing false receiving reports. The company's three-way match control did not detect the scheme. This illustrates which inherent limitation of internal control?
choices: Cost-benefit constraints on control design
Human error in applying a control
Management override of controls
Collusion among two or more individuals
questions.exp: Segregation of duties and matching controls can be circumvented when people in incompatible roles collude, which is an inherent limitation recognized by COSO and AU-C 315. Management override involves managers, not clerks, bypassing controls.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs of duties, if performed by the same employee, represents the most serious weakness in segregation of duties?
choices: Receiving customer payments and posting them to the accounts receivable subsidiary ledger
Preparing the bank deposit and taking it to the bank
Maintaining the general ledger and preparing the trial balance
Preparing a remittance list and restrictively endorsing incoming checks
questions.exp: Combining custody of cash receipts with recording in customer accounts lets an employee steal receipts and conceal the theft, for example through lapping. The other pairs combine duties of the same type, either custody with custody or recording with recording.

questions.q: During a nonissuer audit, the auditor determines that a control deficiency creates a reasonable possibility that a material misstatement of the financial statements will not be prevented, or detected and corrected, on a timely basis. Under AU-C 265, this deficiency is
choices: a material weakness
a control deficiency that need only be communicated orally
a deficiency in design but not in operation
a significant deficiency
questions.exp: AU-C 265 defines a material weakness as a deficiency, or combination of deficiencies, with a reasonable possibility that a material misstatement will not be prevented, or detected and corrected, on a timely basis. A significant deficiency is less severe but still merits the attention of those charged with governance.

questions.q: Under AU-C 265, how and when must the auditor of a nonissuer communicate significant deficiencies and material weaknesses identified during the audit?
choices: In the auditor's report on the financial statements, as an other-matter paragraph
In writing to management only, within 30 days after the report date
Orally to management, before the end of fieldwork
In writing to management and those charged with governance, no later than 60 days following the report release date
questions.exp: AU-C 265 requires written communication of significant deficiencies and material weaknesses to management and those charged with governance, preferably by the report release date and no later than 60 days after it. Oral communication is not enough for these deficiencies, and they are not reported in the opinion.

questions.q: During a nonissuer audit, the auditor identifies several control deficiencies that are neither significant deficiencies nor material weaknesses but are important enough to merit management's attention. Under AU-C 265, the auditor should
choices: include them in the management representation letter
communicate them in writing to those charged with governance within 60 days
not communicate them, because only significant deficiencies and material weaknesses require communication
communicate them to management on a timely basis, either in writing or orally
questions.exp: AU-C 265 requires the auditor to communicate other deficiencies that merit management's attention to management on a timely basis, and oral communication is allowed. The written communication requirement applies only to significant deficiencies and material weaknesses.

questions.q: An auditor finds that the review of journal entries over $50,000 was not performed for three months. No misstatements were found in those entries. Under AU-C 265, how does the absence of an actual misstatement affect the evaluation of the deficiency's severity?
choices: Severity depends on whether there is a reasonable possibility that the control could fail to prevent or detect a misstatement and on the potential magnitude, not on whether a misstatement actually occurred
The deficiency must be classified as a material weakness, because the control was not performed
The deficiency cannot be more than a minor deficiency, because no misstatement occurred
The deficiency need not be evaluated, because substantive procedures found no errors
questions.exp: AU-C 265 states that the severity of a deficiency does not depend on whether a misstatement actually occurred. It depends on the likelihood and potential magnitude of misstatement. An absence of errors in substantive testing does not show that the control is effective.

questions.q: When evaluating the severity of a control deficiency, the auditor identifies a compensating control. Which statement is correct?
choices: A compensating control eliminates the deficiency, so it need not be considered further
Compensating controls increase the severity of the deficiency because they show that controls are redundant
Compensating controls are considered only in audits of issuers

A compensating control may limit the severity of the deficiency if it operates at a level of precision that would prevent, or detect and correct, a material misstatement, but it does not eliminate the deficiency
questions.exp: Under AU-C 265 and AS 2201, effective compensating controls can reduce the severity of a deficiency, for example from a material weakness to a significant deficiency, but the deficiency still exists. To be effective, the compensating control must operate with sufficient precision.

questions.q: Which of the following is an indicator of a material weakness in internal control?
choices: The auditor identifies a material misstatement in the current-period financial statements that the entity's controls would not have detected
Internal audit identifies an immaterial error and management corrects it on a timely basis
The auditor proposes no audit adjustments for the year
The company converts to a new general ledger system during the year
questions.exp: AU-C 265 and AS 2201 list indicators of a material weakness: an auditor-identified material misstatement not detected by the entity's controls, fraud by senior management, a restatement to correct a material misstatement, and ineffective audit committee oversight. An immaterial error that internal controls caught is evidence that controls are working.

questions.q: In an integrated audit under PCAOB AS 2201, the auditor uses a top-down approach to select controls to test. This approach begins with
choices: the financial statement level and the auditor's understanding of overall risks to internal control over financial reporting, then entity-level controls, then significant accounts and relevant assertions
testing the operating effectiveness of each transaction-level control in the significant processes
the controls that management has identified as most costly to operate
the IT general controls over every application in the company
questions.exp: AS 2201 describes a top-down approach that starts at the financial statement level, considers entity-level controls, and then moves to significant accounts, disclosures, and relevant assertions. Only then does the auditor select transaction-level controls. Starting with every transaction-level control is the bottom-up approach the standard moves away from.

questions.q: In an integrated audit of an issuer with a December 31 year-end, the auditor identifies a material weakness that existed at December 31. Management fully remediates the weakness in February, before the auditor's report is issued, and the auditor confirms the remediated control is working. Under PCAOB AS 2201, the auditor's opinion on internal control over financial reporting should be
choices: a disclaimer, because the remediation creates a scope limitation
adverse, because the material weakness existed as of December 31
unmodified, because the weakness was remediated before the report date
qualified, with a paragraph describing the remediation
questions.exp: The ICFR opinion is as of the assessment date, December 31. A material weakness that existed at that date requires an adverse opinion even if it is remediated afterward. AS 2201 does not permit a qualified opinion because of a material weakness.

questions.q: In an integrated audit, the auditor identifies an entity-level control in which management reviews detailed monthly results by product line and investigates differences from expectations. If this control monitors other controls and operates at a level of precision that would adequately prevent or detect material misstatements, the auditor may
choices: reduce the testing of other controls related to the relevant assertions
conclude that no walkthroughs are needed for any process
eliminate all testing of controls in the related processes and all substantive procedures
not consider the control, because entity-level controls are relevant only to the control environment
questions.exp: AS 2201 notes that precise entity-level controls can sufficiently address the risk for an assertion, which allows the auditor to reduce testing of other controls. Substantive procedures for material accounts are always required, so eliminating them would be wrong.

questions.q: In obtaining an understanding of internal control in a financial statement audit, the auditor wants to determine whether a control over credit approval has been implemented. Under AU-C 315, which approach is appropriate?
choices: Perform procedures in addition to inquiry, such as observing the control or inspecting documents showing its application
Inquiry of the credit manager alone is sufficient
Obtain a written representation from management that the control exists
Rely on the prior-year conclusion if the control was implemented last year
questions.exp: AU-C 315 states that inquiry alone is not sufficient to evaluate design and determine implementation. The auditor combines inquiry with observation, inspection, or a walkthrough. Management representations do not replace that evidence.

questions.q: Under AU-C 315, as amended by SAS No. 145, which of the following controls must the auditor identify and evaluate for design and implementation, even if the auditor does not plan to test its operating effectiveness?
choices: Controls over the efficiency of production scheduling
All controls in every business process
Controls over journal entries, including nonstandard journal entries
Controls that management considers least important
questions.exp: SAS No. 145 requires the auditor to identify controls over journal entries, controls that address significant risks, controls the auditor plans to test, and others in its judgment, and to evaluate their design and implementation. Operational efficiency controls are generally not relevant, and not all controls in every process must be identified.

questions.q: Before a batch of payroll time records is processed, the computer totals the employee identification numbers in the batch and compares the result with a total computed manually when the batch was prepared. This control is primarily designed to detect
choices: employees paid at an incorrect wage rate
hours worked that exceed a reasonable limit
payroll charged to the wrong department
missing, added, or altered records in the batch
questions.exp: A hash total is a sum of a field with no meaning in itself, such as ID numbers, and it changes if records are lost, added, or altered between preparation and processing. Wage rates and hour limits are addressed by validity checks and limit tests.

questions.q: Which of the following is a detective control rather than a preventive control?
choices: Using passwords to restrict access to the vendor master file
Requiring credit approval before goods are shipped to customers
A monthly bank reconciliation prepared by an employee independent of cash handling and recording
Requiring two authorized signatures on checks over $10,000
questions.exp: A bank reconciliation identifies errors or irregularities after they have occurred, which makes it a detective control. Dual signatures, credit approval, and access restrictions operate before a transaction is completed to prevent misstatements.

questions.q: A small nonissuer has only two accounting employees, so complete segregation of duties is not practical. Which of the following is most likely to mitigate the risk created by the lack of segregation?
choices: Increasing the number of journal entries recorded each month
Having the external auditor perform the bank reconciliations
Active involvement of the owner-manager in approving disbursements and reviewing bank statements and reconciliations
Rotating the two employees' duties every month
questions.exp: AU-C 315 recognizes that in smaller entities, an owner-manager's direct involvement can compensate for limited segregation of duties, although it increases the risk of management override. The external auditor performing client controls would impair independence and is not an entity control.

questions.q: Which controls are generally relevant to a financial statement audit?
choices: Primarily controls related to financial reporting objectives, although some operations or compliance controls may be relevant if they relate to data the auditor uses
Only controls over compliance with laws and regulations
All controls in the entity, regardless of objective
Only controls over the efficiency and effectiveness of operations
questions.exp: COSO's objectives are operations, reporting, and compliance. Controls related to financial reporting are generally relevant to an audit. Operations and compliance controls are relevant only when they affect data the auditor evaluates or uses in procedures, for example production statistics used in analytics.

questions.q: Under COSO's Enterprise Risk Management-Integrating with Strategy and Performance (2017), defining the organization's risk appetite belongs to which component?
choices: Information, Communication, and Reporting
Strategy and Objective-Setting
Governance and Culture
Review and Revision
questions.exp: The 2017 COSO ERM framework places defining risk appetite under Strategy and Objective-Setting, alongside analyzing business context and formulating business objectives. Governance and Culture covers board oversight, operating structures, and core values instead.

questions.q: At the end of a nonissuer audit, the auditor identified no material weaknesses and no significant deficiencies. Management asks for a letter stating that no significant deficiencies were identified. Under AU-C 265, the auditor
choices: must issue the letter to those charged with governance
should not issue a written communication stating that no significant deficiencies were identified
may issue the letter only if the auditor tested all controls
may issue the letter if it is restricted to management's use
questions.exp: AU-C 265 prohibits a written communication stating that no significant deficiencies were identified, because users could misunderstand the limited assurance involved. A communication stating that no material weaknesses were identified is permitted, which is why the request for a no-significant-deficiency letter is a trap.

questions.q: In an integrated audit under PCAOB AS 2201, as the risk associated with a control increases, the auditor's use of the work of internal auditors and others to test that control should
choices: increase, because more evidence is needed
remain the same, because the work of others is evaluated only on competence
decrease, with the auditor performing more of the work
be eliminated only for controls that operate monthly
questions.exp: AS 2201 states that as the risk associated with a control increases, the auditor should rely less on the work of others and perform more of the work personally. Competence and objectivity of the others also matter, but risk is a separate factor that limits use.

questions.q: An auditor wants to document its understanding of the sales and cash receipts process in a form that clearly shows the flow of documents, the processing steps, and the separation of duties among departments. Which form of documentation is best suited to this purpose?
choices: A listing of all controls tested in the prior year
A systems flowchart
A narrative memorandum
An internal control questionnaire with yes or no answers
questions.exp: A flowchart shows the sequence of documents and processing across departments, which makes gaps in segregation of duties and missing controls easier to see. Questionnaires are efficient for spotting missing controls but do not show the flow of transactions.

questions.q: In a financial statement audit of a nonissuer, what is the auditor's responsibility for identifying deficiencies in internal control?
choices: The auditor must communicate deficiencies identified during the audit but is not required to perform procedures designed to identify all deficiencies
The auditor must perform procedures sufficient to express an opinion on internal control
The auditor must test every control relevant to financial reporting to identify all deficiencies
The auditor has no responsibility regarding control deficiencies
questions.exp: In a financial statement audit, the auditor considers internal control to design audit procedures, not to opine on it. AU-C 265 requires communication of deficiencies that come to the auditor's attention, but not a search for all deficiencies. An ICFR opinion requires a separate examination or an integrated audit.

questions.q: In an integrated audit, the auditor performs a walkthrough of the purchasing process. Under PCAOB AS 2201, which is a primary objective of a walkthrough?
choices: To select a statistical sample of purchase transactions for testing
To provide sufficient evidence of operating effectiveness for the entire year
To understand the flow of transactions, verify the points at which misstatements could occur, and evaluate the design and implementation of controls
To replace substantive tests of accounts payable
questions.exp: AS 2201 describes walkthroughs, which follow a transaction from origination through processing and recording, as a way to achieve objectives such as understanding the flow of transactions, identifying where misstatements could occur, and evaluating control design. A single walkthrough does not establish operating effectiveness over the period.

questions.q: A CPA is engaged to prepare a nonissuer's financial statements under AR-C 70 and will not issue a compilation report. Which is required?
choices: Each page of the financial statements must include a statement that no assurance is provided, or a disclaimer must be issued
The CPA must obtain a management representation letter
The CPA must be independent of the entity
A compilation report must be attached
questions.exp: AR-C 70 requires that each page indicate 'no assurance is provided'; if that is not possible, the accountant issues a disclaimer, or else performs a compilation instead. Independence is not required for a preparation engagement, and no report or representation letter is required.

questions.q: A CPA performing a compilation under AR-C 80 is not independent of the client. Which is correct?
choices: The CPA must issue a review report instead
The CPA must withdraw because compilations require independence
The CPA may issue the report but must disclose the lack of independence in a final paragraph, and may optionally describe the reasons
The CPA must convert the engagement to a preparation engagement
questions.exp: AR-C 80 permits a compilation when the accountant is not independent, but the report must disclose the impairment; reasons may be described, and if any are described, all must be. Independence is required for reviews, not compilations.

questions.q: Which of the following procedures is required in a review engagement under AR-C 90?
choices: Analytical procedures and inquiries designed to accumulate review evidence for obtaining limited assurance
Observation of inventory
Tests of controls over cash disbursements
Confirmation of receivables
questions.exp: A review consists primarily of analytical procedures and inquiries to obtain limited assurance. Confirmation, observation, and tests of controls are audit procedures not required in a review.

questions.q: Which of the following is a required element of a review engagement under AR-C 90 but not of a compilation under AR-C 80?
choices: An engagement letter signed by the accountant and management
A requirement to read the financial statements
A report signed by the accountant
A written representation letter from management
questions.exp: AR-C 90 requires written representations from management; AR-C 80 does not. Both engagements require an engagement letter and a signed report, and the accountant reads the statements in both.

questions.q: A client asks the CPA to review financial statements that omit substantially all disclosures required by GAAP. Under SSARS, the CPA should:
choices: Perform the review and add an emphasis-of-matter paragraph
Perform the review and issue an unmodified conclusion with a paragraph noting the omission
Not accept the review engagement on those financial statements
Perform the review and issue a qualified conclusion
questions.exp: SSARS permit preparation and compilation of statements omitting substantially all disclosures (with appropriate indication), but a review of such statements is not permitted. Issuing a review report would imply limited assurance on statements that are incomplete.

questions.q: Under SSARS 25, if a CPA performing a review concludes that the financial statements contain a material misstatement whose effects are both material and pervasive, the CPA should:
choices: Issue an adverse conclusion
Issue an unmodified conclusion with an emphasis-of-matter paragraph
Disclaim a conclusion
Issue a qualified conclusion
questions.exp: SSARS 25 introduced adverse conclusions for misstatements that are material and pervasive, with qualified conclusions for misstatements that are material but not pervasive. A review accountant cannot disclaim a conclusion; inability to complete the review leads to withdrawal.

questions.q: During a review, management refuses to provide written representations. Under AR-C 90, the accountant should:
choices: Issue a compilation report instead without any further consideration
Not issue a review report, because a review cannot be completed without the representations, and consider withdrawing
Issue a qualified conclusion
Issue a review report with a disclaimer of conclusion
questions.exp: A review is incomplete without written representations, and SSARS do not permit a disclaimer in a review; the accountant cannot issue a review report and should withdraw. Changing to a compilation requires considering the reason, and a refusal to provide representations generally argues against simply issuing a compilation report.

questions.q: Which of the following is true regarding materiality in a review engagement under SSARS 25?
choices: Materiality is applied only to the presentation of disclosures
The accountant is required to determine materiality for the financial statements as a whole and apply it in designing procedures and evaluating results
Materiality must equal planning materiality used in a hypothetical audit
The accountant is not permitted to consider materiality
questions.exp: SSARS 25 requires the accountant to determine materiality for the financial statements as a whole and apply it in designing procedures and evaluating misstatements. There is no requirement that review materiality equal audit materiality.

questions.q: A CPA engaged to audit a nonissuer's statements is asked midway through to change to a review. The CPA learns that management refused to allow the CPA to correspond with the entity's legal counsel. Which is most appropriate?
choices: Change to a review and issue the report without considering the reason
The CPA ordinarily would be precluded from issuing a review report
Issue an audit report with a disclaimer and a review report
Change to a review and refer to the original audit engagement in the review report
questions.exp: SSARS note that when management refuses to allow correspondence with legal counsel, the accountant ordinarily would be precluded from issuing a review or compilation report. Even when a change is acceptable, the report should not refer to the original engagement.

questions.q: A CPA reviews a nonissuer's financial statements and identifies conditions raising substantial doubt about going concern; management's disclosures are adequate. The review report should:
choices: Express an adverse conclusion
Omit any reference because reviews do not address going concern
Express a qualified conclusion
Include an emphasis-of-matter paragraph about the going concern uncertainty
questions.exp: AR-C 90 requires the accountant to consider going concern and, when substantial doubt exists and disclosure is adequate, to include an emphasis-of-matter paragraph. A modified conclusion would apply only if disclosure were inadequate.

questions.q: When does AR-C 70 (preparation of financial statements) apply?
choices: Whenever a CPA performs bookkeeping, even if not engaged to prepare financial statements
When the accountant is engaged to prepare financial statements
Only when the financial statements are to be submitted to a third party
Whenever a CPA prepares a tax return
questions.exp: AR-C 70 applies when the accountant is engaged to prepare financial statements, regardless of intended users. It does not apply to tax returns or to bookkeeping services when the accountant is not engaged to prepare financial statements.

questions.q: A CPA compiles financial statements prepared on the tax basis of accounting. Under AR-C 80, the compilation report should:
choices: Include a paragraph stating that the statements are prepared on the tax basis, referring to the note that describes that basis, and stating that it is a basis of accounting other than GAAP
State that the accountant audited the tax basis adjustments
Express limited assurance that the statements are prepared in accordance with the tax basis
Restrict use to the IRS
questions.exp: AR-C 80 requires the compilation report on special purpose framework statements to include a paragraph stating the framework, referring to the note describing it, and stating it is a basis other than GAAP. Compilations provide no assurance, and tax-basis statements are not restricted to the IRS.

questions.q: Which statement best describes the level of assurance provided in compilation and review engagements under SSARS?
choices: A compilation provides limited assurance, and a review provides reasonable assurance
Both provide limited assurance
Both provide no assurance
A compilation provides no assurance, and a review provides limited assurance
questions.exp: A compilation provides no assurance, while a review provides limited assurance that no material modifications are needed. Reasonable assurance is provided only by an audit or examination.

questions.q: During a review, the accountant's analytical procedures reveal that gross margin rose sharply despite flat sales and rising input costs. Management's explanation is vague. The accountant should:
choices: Perform additional procedures to obtain limited assurance that no material modification is needed
Convert to an audit
Accept management's explanation because a review consists of inquiries
Issue an adverse conclusion immediately
questions.exp: When the accountant becomes aware of information that the statements may be materially misstated, AR-C 90 requires additional procedures sufficient to achieve limited assurance. Accepting a vague explanation is insufficient, and an adverse conclusion is premature.

questions.q: Under SSARS, which item must be included in the engagement letter for a compilation?
choices: The fee arrangement only
A statement that the accountant will detect all fraud
An agreement to perform audit procedures if needed
The objective, management's responsibilities, the accountant's responsibilities, the limitations, the applicable framework, and the expected form of report
questions.exp: AR-C 80 requires an engagement letter documenting objectives, responsibilities, limitations (including that the engagement cannot be relied on to detect fraud), the framework, and the expected report. Compilations do not detect fraud or include audit procedures.

questions.q: A CPA reviews a nonissuer's financial statements and also prepares the client's payroll and adjusting entries. Under the AICPA Code, which is most accurate?
choices: The CPA must disclose the services in the review report
Independence is automatically impaired by preparing adjusting entries
Independence is not relevant to a review
Independence may be maintained if the general requirements for nonattest services are met and threats are reduced to an acceptable level, including evaluating the self-review threat
questions.exp: The Code permits nonattest services for attest clients if management takes responsibility and safeguards are applied; significant threats are evaluated under the conceptual framework. Independence is required for a review, and nonattest services are not disclosed in the report.

questions.q: Which document must a CPA obtain in a review that is not required in a compilation?
choices: A representation letter addressed to the accountant
A confirmation of the bank balance
A legal letter from the client's attorney
A signed copy of the tax return
questions.exp: AR-C 90 requires written representations from management. Legal letters and confirmations are audit procedures not required in either SSARS engagement.

questions.q: A CPA performing a compilation discovers that the financial statements contain a material departure from GAAP that management will not correct. The CPA should:
choices: Ignore the departure because a compilation provides no assurance
Issue an adverse conclusion
Issue a qualified opinion
Disclose the departure in the compilation report if the CPA does not withdraw
questions.exp: AR-C 80 requires the accountant to disclose a known departure in a separate paragraph of the compilation report, or to withdraw if modification is not adequate. Opinions and conclusions do not apply to compilations.

questions.q: Which of the following is true of a review report on a nonissuer's financial statements under SSARS?
choices: It is dated as of the balance sheet date
It expresses an opinion on internal control
It includes a statement that the accountant is not independent if that is the case
It is dated no earlier than the date the accountant obtained sufficient appropriate review evidence
questions.exp: AR-C 90 requires the review report to be dated no earlier than the date sufficient appropriate review evidence was obtained. An accountant who is not independent cannot issue a review report, and reviews provide no assurance on internal control.

questions.q: A CPA performs a review of a nonissuer's annual statements and identifies a material misstatement that is not pervasive. Management will not correct it. Under SSARS 25, the review report should:
choices: Express an adverse conclusion
Disclaim a conclusion
Express an unmodified conclusion with an emphasis-of-matter paragraph
Express a qualified conclusion with a basis for qualified conclusion section
questions.exp: SSARS 25 requires a qualified conclusion for misstatements that are material but not pervasive, with the basis described. An adverse conclusion is for material and pervasive misstatements.

questions.q: A CPA who audits a nonissuer's annual financial statements is engaged to review its quarterly interim financial information. Which standard applies to the interim review?
choices: AR-C 90, Review of Financial Statements
AU-C 930, Interim Financial Information
AT-C 210, Review Engagements
PCAOB AS 4105
questions.exp: AU-C 930 applies to reviews of interim financial information when the auditor audits the entity's most recent annual statements and certain conditions are met. AR-C 90 applies to reviews where the accountant is not engaged in that circumstance.

questions.q: Under AR-C 70, which statement is correct?
choices: The accountant must issue a report
The accountant must determine independence
The accountant must perform analytical procedures
The accountant is required to obtain an engagement letter signed by the accountant and management
questions.exp: AR-C 70 requires a signed engagement letter but does not require a report, analytical procedures, or a determination of independence. Those requirements arise in compilations (report) and reviews (procedures, independence).

questions.q: A CPA performs a compilation of statements that include supplementary information. The CPA's report should:
choices: Express an opinion on the supplementary information in relation to the statements
Express limited assurance on the supplementary information
Ignore the supplementary information
Indicate the degree of responsibility, if any, the accountant is taking with respect to the supplementary information
questions.exp: SSARS require the accountant to clarify the degree of responsibility taken for supplementary information accompanying compiled statements. Compilations provide no assurance, so neither limited assurance nor an opinion applies.

questions.q: In a review engagement, which of the following inquiries would most likely be made of management?
choices: Inquiries about significant journal entries, subsequent events, and actions authorized by the board
Inquiries of the entity's bank about loan terms
Inquiries of the client's customers about receivable balances
Inquiries of the entity's legal counsel about litigation
questions.exp: AR-C 90 inquiries are directed to management and those with responsibility for financial matters, such as about unusual or complex situations, subsequent events, and board actions. Inquiries of third parties are generally audit procedures.

questions.q: A CPA is asked to perform a review of statements of a nonissuer but discovers the CPA has a direct financial interest in the client. The CPA should:
choices: Issue a qualified conclusion
Not perform the review, though the CPA could perform a compilation with disclosure of the lack of independence
Perform the review and disclose the lack of independence
Perform the review without disclosure if the interest is immaterial
questions.exp: Independence is required to issue a review report under AR-C 90, and a direct financial interest impairs independence regardless of materiality. A compilation can still be performed with disclosure of the impairment.

questions.q: Which statement regarding documentation in a review engagement under SSARS is correct?
choices: Documentation should include the engagement letter, significant findings, communications with management, expectations for analytics where significant, and the representation letter
Documentation must include tests of controls
Documentation must include confirmation responses
No documentation is required because the report is the documentation
questions.exp: AR-C 90 documentation includes the engagement letter, analytical procedures and results, significant findings, communications, and the representation letter. Tests of controls and confirmations are not review procedures.

questions.q: A CPA performing a review becomes aware of an instance of noncompliance with laws that may have a material effect. Which is most appropriate?
choices: Obtain an understanding of the matter, discuss it with management, consider its effect on the financial statements and the review report, and communicate as appropriate
Ignore it because a review does not address compliance
Report it directly to the regulator immediately
Issue an adverse conclusion
questions.exp: SSARS require the accountant who becomes aware of noncompliance to obtain an understanding, discuss with management and TCWG as appropriate, and evaluate the effect on the statements and report. External reporting is generally not required absent legal obligations.

questions.q: A CPA has compiled a client's statements and the client wants to include the compiled statements in a document with audited statements of a prior year. Which consideration is most relevant?
choices: The CPA must reaudit the prior year
Each period's report should describe the level of service on that period, and the current-period compilation report must not imply assurance
No report is needed on the compiled period
The compiled statements automatically become audited
questions.exp: When periods with different levels of service are presented comparatively, the reports must clearly reflect the service for each period. Compilation does not convert into an audit and still requires a report.

questions.q: During a compilation, the accountant becomes aware that records supporting a material balance are incomplete. Management refuses to provide the additional information requested. Under AR-C 80, the accountant should:
choices: Perform audit procedures to verify the balance
Issue the compilation report without modification because compilations provide no assurance
Issue the compilation report with a qualified opinion
Withdraw from the engagement and inform management of the reasons
questions.exp: AR-C 80 requires the accountant to request additional or revised information when records are incorrect or incomplete, and to withdraw if management does not provide it. Compilations provide no assurance, but that does not permit association with statements the accountant knows may be materially misstated.

questions.q: A CPA newly engaged to review a manufacturer's statements has no prior experience in that industry. What knowledge must the CPA obtain before designing the review procedures?
choices: Assessing the risk of material misstatement due to fraud as in an audit
Inspecting documents supporting a sample of transactions in each account
Obtaining an understanding of the industry and of the entity's accounting principles and practices sufficient to design analytical procedures and inquiries
Obtaining an understanding of internal control sufficient to assess control risk
questions.exp: AR-C 90 requires knowledge of the industry and of the entity, including its accounting principles and practices, to design review procedures. Assessing control risk, audit-level fraud risk assessments, and routine document inspection are audit procedures not required in a review.

topics.topic: Subsequent events and subsequently discovered facts

questions.q: After a December 31 year-end but before the auditor's report date, a major customer files for bankruptcy because of a steady deterioration in its financial condition over the prior two years. The receivable is material. How should the entity reflect this event?
choices: Disclose the event only, without adjustment
Neither adjust nor disclose because it occurred after year-end
Adjust next year's financial statements
Adjust the allowance for credit losses at December 31
questions.exp: Because the customer's financial deterioration existed at the balance sheet date, the bankruptcy provides evidence about conditions at year-end and is a recognized (Type 1) subsequent event requiring adjustment. Disclosure only applies to conditions arising after the balance sheet date.

questions.q: After year-end but before the financial statements are available to be issued, a fire destroys a nonissuer's main warehouse, causing a material uninsured loss. The financial statements should:
choices: Ignore the loss because it occurred after year-end
Be adjusted only if the loss exceeds 10% of total assets
Disclose the loss without adjusting year-end balances
Be adjusted to record the loss at year-end
questions.exp: A fire after year-end is a condition that arose after the balance sheet date, a nonrecognized (Type 2) subsequent event requiring disclosure if material but not adjustment. Recording the loss at year-end would misstate the conditions that existed then.

questions.q: Which procedure is an auditor of a nonissuer required to perform to identify subsequent events under AU-C 560?
choices: Confirm all year-end receivables again at the report date
Reperform year-end cutoff tests at the report date
Read minutes of meetings of owners, management, and those charged with governance held after the period end and inquire about matters discussed at meetings for which minutes are not yet available
Obtain a legal letter dated after the report release date
questions.exp: AU-C 560 requires procedures such as understanding management's procedures, inquiry, reading minutes (and inquiring about meetings without minutes), and reading the latest interim financial statements. Reconfirming receivables is not a required subsequent events procedure.

questions.q: Through what date is the auditor of a nonissuer required to perform procedures designed to identify subsequent events requiring adjustment or disclosure?
choices: The date of the auditor's report, or as near as practicable
The end of the look-forward period for going concern
The balance sheet date
The date the financial statements are released to users
questions.exp: AU-C 560 requires the auditor to perform procedures covering the period from the financial statement date to the date of the auditor's report (or as near as practicable). After the report date, the auditor has no obligation to perform procedures unless facts become known.

questions.q: After the auditor's report date but before the report is released, the auditor becomes aware of a fact that, had it been known at the report date, might have caused the auditor to revise the report. The auditor should first:
choices: Release the report as originally dated because no further obligation exists
Withdraw from the engagement
Notify regulators that the report cannot be relied upon
Discuss the matter with management and, where appropriate, those charged with governance, and determine whether the financial statements need revision
questions.exp: AU-C 560 requires discussion with management and determination of whether the financial statements need revision when the auditor becomes aware of such facts before release. Withdrawal or regulatory notification is not the first step.

questions.q: Six months after issuing an unmodified report, the auditor of a nonissuer discovers that the client's year-end inventory included goods consigned from others, a material error that existed at the report date. The auditor should first:
choices: Discuss the matter with management and, where appropriate, those charged with governance, and determine whether the financial statements need revision
Disregard the matter because the report has been released
Issue a revised report without involving management
Recall the report directly from all known users without contacting the client
questions.exp: Under AU-C 560, when facts that existed at the report date are discovered after release, the auditor discusses the matter with management and TCWG and determines whether the financial statements need revision, and if so inquires how management intends to address it. Ignoring material subsequently discovered facts is inappropriate.

questions.q: Management agrees to revise previously issued financial statements for a subsequently discovered fact. What is the auditor's responsibility?
choices: Perform procedures limited only to reading the revised note
Issue a letter stating the original report is withdrawn, without further procedures
Require that the entity change auditors
Perform necessary audit procedures on the revision, and issue a new or revised report including an emphasis-of-matter or other-matter paragraph referencing the reason for revision
questions.exp: AU-C 560 requires the auditor to perform procedures on the revision and provide a new or revised report, with an emphasis-of-matter or other-matter paragraph describing the reason for the revision and referring to the note. The auditor also considers whether management communicated with users.

questions.q: Management refuses to take steps to inform users that previously issued financial statements should no longer be relied upon after a subsequently discovered material error. After notifying management and those charged with governance, the auditor should:
choices: Take appropriate action to seek to prevent further reliance on the auditor's report, considering legal advice
Take no further action because confidentiality prohibits disclosure
Issue a new adverse opinion and send it only to management
Wait until the next year's audit to address the matter
questions.exp: AU-C 560 requires the auditor, after notifying management and TCWG, to take action to seek to prevent future reliance on the report, which may include notifying regulators and known users, often with legal counsel. Doing nothing leaves users relying on a report the auditor knows is unsupported.

questions.q: A predecessor auditor is asked to reissue its report on prior-year statements that will be presented comparatively with the current year audited by a successor. Before reissuing, the predecessor should:
choices: Redate the report to the successor's report date
Reaudit the prior period in full
Rely solely on the successor's report
Read the current-period financial statements, compare the prior-period statements to those previously issued, and obtain representation letters from management and the successor auditor
questions.exp: AU-C 560 lists these procedures for a predecessor reissuing its report, including written representations from management and the successor. The predecessor generally uses its original report date unless dual dating for a revision.

questions.q: A nonissuer issues common stock in a public offering after year-end but before the financial statements are available to be issued. The financial statements should:
choices: Present a pro forma balance sheet in place of the historical balance sheet
Ignore the issuance
Record the issuance as of year-end
Disclose the issuance as a nonrecognized subsequent event
questions.exp: Issuance of stock after year-end relates to conditions arising after the balance sheet date, so it is disclosed but not recognized. Pro forma data may supplement, but does not replace, historical statements.

questions.q: Lawsuit damages based on an event that occurred before year-end are settled after year-end, before the statements are available to be issued, for an amount materially greater than the accrual. Which treatment is appropriate?
choices: Adjust the year-end accrual to reflect the settlement amount
Reverse the accrual and disclose the settlement
Recognize the gain or loss in the following year
Disclose only, because the settlement occurred after year-end
questions.exp: Settlement of litigation arising from an event before year-end provides additional evidence about conditions at the balance sheet date, so it is a recognized subsequent event and the accrual is adjusted (ASC 855). Disclosure only applies if the underlying event occurred after year-end.

questions.q: When the auditor reissues a report on financial statements that were not revised and no new events require disclosure, the reissued report should be dated:
choices: As of the reissuance date
As of the end of the current year
As of the date the client requests reissuance
As of the original report date
questions.exp: A reissued report uses the original date to avoid implying that subsequent events procedures were performed after that date (AU-C 560). Redating would extend the auditor's responsibility to the new date.

questions.q: After issuing the report, an auditor discovers that a confirmation procedure considered necessary at the time was omitted, and the auditor's other procedures do not compensate. Users are believed to be relying on the report. Under AU-C 585, the auditor should:
choices: Notify the state board of accountancy
Withdraw the report immediately without further procedures
Disregard the omission because the report was already issued
Promptly undertake to apply the omitted procedure or alternative procedures that would provide a satisfactory basis for the opinion
questions.exp: AU-C 585 requires the auditor, if the omission impairs the ability to support the opinion and users are relying on it, to promptly perform the omitted or alternative procedures. Withdrawal is considered only if procedures reveal the statements are misstated or the auditor cannot apply them.

questions.q: Which of the following is a subsequent event that ordinarily requires disclosure but not adjustment?
choices: A business combination completed after year-end
Discovery after year-end of an inventory obsolescence condition that existed at year-end
Collection of a receivable at an amount different from the year-end estimate due to conditions existing at year-end
Determination after year-end of the final sales price of goods sold before year-end
questions.exp: A business combination after year-end does not provide evidence about conditions at the balance sheet date, so it is disclosed, not recognized. The other items provide evidence of conditions at year-end and require adjustment.

questions.q: Management's written representations should be dated:
choices: As of the balance sheet date
As of the date financial statements are issued
As near as practicable to, but not after, the date of the auditor's report
As of the date the fieldwork began
questions.exp: AU-C 580 requires written representations to be dated as near as practicable to, but not after, the date of the auditor's report, so they cover the subsequent events period. Dating them at the balance sheet date would not cover events through the report date.

questions.q: An auditor of a nonissuer dual-dated the report for a subsequent event disclosed in Note 12. For which period is the auditor responsible for subsequent events?
choices: Through the release date for all events
Through the original report date for all events, and through the later date only for the event described in Note 12
Through the later date for all events
Only through the balance sheet date
questions.exp: Dual dating limits the auditor's responsibility for events after the original report date to the specific event disclosed (AU-C 560). Redating, by contrast, extends responsibility for all events to the later date.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the auditor's responsibility for facts that become known after the report is released?
choices: The auditor must perform quarterly inquiries of management after release
The auditor must continue performing subsequent events procedures for one year after release
The auditor's responsibility ends permanently at the report date
The auditor has no obligation to perform procedures after release, but if a fact becomes known that would have caused revision of the report, the auditor must respond
questions.exp: AU-C 560 provides no obligation to perform procedures after release, but when facts become known that existed at the report date and might have affected the report, the auditor must take the steps prescribed. The responsibility is reactive, not continuous.

questions.q: Which subsequent event would most likely require a nonissuer to adjust its year-end financial statements?
choices: Sale of inventory after year-end at a price below cost that reflects conditions of obsolescence existing at year-end
Entering into a significant purchase commitment after year-end
A decline in the market value of investments due to a market crash after year-end
A loss on a plant destroyed by flood after year-end
questions.exp: Sales after year-end below cost that reflect obsolescence existing at year-end provide evidence of net realizable value at the balance sheet date and require adjustment. Market declines, floods, and new commitments after year-end are nonrecognized events.

questions.q: A nonissuer's financial statements were revised after release due to a subsequently discovered fact. In the new auditor's report, the auditor should:
choices: Omit any reference to the earlier report
Include an adverse opinion on the original statements
Date the new report no earlier than the date the revised statements are approved and include an explanatory paragraph describing the revision
Use the original report date only, with no explanatory paragraph
questions.exp: Under AU-C 560, the new or revised report is dated no earlier than the date of approval of the revised statements (or dual dated) and includes an emphasis-of-matter or other-matter paragraph referring to the note describing the revision. An adverse opinion is not appropriate for statements that have been properly revised.

questions.q: For an issuer audit under PCAOB standards, which standard addresses the auditor's responsibilities when facts existing at the report date are discovered after the report has been issued?
choices: AS 2801, Subsequent Events
AS 2201, An Audit of ICFR
AS 3101, The Auditor's Report
AS 2905, Subsequent Discovery of Facts Existing at the Date of the Auditor's Report
questions.exp: AS 2905 addresses subsequently discovered facts after the report date for issuers. AS 2801 covers subsequent events through the report date.

questions.q: An auditor issued an unmodified report in March. In June, the auditor learns of a customer's bankruptcy filed in May that resulted from a fire in April. Which is the auditor's responsibility?
choices: Issue a revised report with dual dating
No action is required because the event did not exist at the report date
Discuss with management whether the statements require revision
Notify users that the report should not be relied upon
