questions.exp: AU-C 560's subsequently discovered facts requirements apply only to facts that existed at the report date; a bankruptcy caused by an April fire arose after the March report. No revision of the issued statements is required.

questions.q: In the current-year audit, the auditor learns of a fact that would have changed the prior-year report, and comparative statements are being issued. Which approach is appropriate under AU-C 560?
choices: Disclaim on the prior year only
Issue an adverse opinion on the current year
Ensure the prior-period statements are revised as appropriate and include an other-matter or emphasis-of-matter paragraph in the current report on comparatives as needed
Report on the current year only and ignore the prior year
questions.exp: When a subsequently discovered fact affects prior statements that are presented comparatively, the prior statements are revised and the auditor's report on the comparatives explains the revision. The current-year opinion is not automatically affected.

questions.q: Which of the following is most likely to be a source of evidence about subsequent events through the report date?
choices: The predecessor auditor's report
The engagement letter
The entity's latest available interim financial statements and inquiries of management about matters since year-end
The prior-year working papers
questions.exp: AU-C 560 requires reading the latest interim statements and inquiring of management about subsequent events. Prior-year papers, the engagement letter, and predecessor reports do not provide information about events after year-end.

questions.q: An auditor of a nonissuer completed fieldwork and dated the report March 1. On April 10, after release, the auditor is asked to provide a report for use in a lender package with no changes to the financial statements. No new events requiring disclosure have come to the auditor's attention. The auditor should:
choices: Reissue the report dated March 1
Perform a new audit
Redate the report to April 10 and perform no procedures
Dual-date the report for the lender package
questions.exp: Reissuing an unchanged report uses the original date (AU-C 560). Redating without procedures would improperly imply responsibility for events through April 10.

questions.q: Which of the following subsequent events requires the auditor's attention most directly because it may require adjustment to the financial statements?
choices: Settlement after year-end of income tax litigation relating to prior years at an amount different from the recorded liability
Changes in exchange rates after year-end
Loss of a major customer after year-end due to a competitor's new product
Declaration of a cash dividend after year-end
questions.exp: Settlement of tax litigation relating to prior years gives evidence about a liability that existed at year-end, requiring adjustment. Dividends declared, customer losses from new events, and post-year-end exchange rate changes are nonrecognized events.

questions.q: After the report release date, an auditor discovers that the client's lawyer had information about an unasserted claim existing at year-end that would have materially changed the financial statements. The auditor determines that persons are relying on the financial statements. Management will not revise. Which is the correct sequence?
choices: Wait one year and reflect it in the next report
Issue a revised report without management's involvement
Notify the SEC first, then management
Notify management and those charged with governance, then take steps to prevent further reliance on the report
questions.exp: AU-C 560 requires the auditor to notify management and TCWG that they should not rely on the report; if they still do not act, the auditor takes appropriate action to prevent further reliance. The auditor cannot unilaterally revise the entity's financial statements.

questions.q: For a nonissuer, the date through which the entity evaluates subsequent events under U.S. GAAP is most typically:
choices: The date the financial statements are available to be issued
The balance sheet date
The date of the annual meeting
The auditor's report date in all cases
questions.exp: Under ASC 855, nonissuers (other than conduit bond obligors) evaluate subsequent events through the date the financial statements are available to be issued and disclose that date. Issuers evaluate through the issuance date.

questions.q: A nonissuer's auditor reissues a report on prior-year financial statements included in a subsequent document, and a subsequent event since the original report date requires disclosure in the statements. How should the reissued report be dated?
choices: Dual-dated, using the original date and a later date for the note disclosing the event
As of the reissuance date for the entire report
As of the balance sheet date
As of the original report date with no reference to the event
questions.exp: AU-C 560 requires a reissued report to be dual dated when the statements are revised to disclose a subsequent event, limiting the later date to the specific note. Redating the entire report extends responsibility for all events.

questions.q: Under PCAOB standards, in which situation must the auditor of an issuer extend subsequent events procedures beyond the original report date?
choices: When the issuer distributes the annual report to shareholders
When the auditor issues a management letter
When the issuer releases quarterly earnings
When an issuer includes the auditor's report in a registration statement filed under the Securities Act of 1933
questions.exp: Under PCAOB AS 4101, inclusion of the auditor's report in a 1933 Act registration statement requires the auditor to perform subsequent events procedures to (or close to) the effective date. Routine distributions and earnings releases do not.

questions.q: During subsequent events procedures, the auditor learns that management signed an agreement after year-end to sell a business segment, and the segment's assets were not impaired at year-end. How should the auditor evaluate the financial statements?
choices: Evaluate whether the agreement is adequately disclosed as a nonrecognized subsequent event
Ignore the agreement because it relates to the next period
Require the segment to be presented as discontinued operations at year-end
Require the assets to be written down to the sales price at year-end
questions.exp: A sale agreement entered into after year-end reflects a decision arising after the balance sheet date, so it is a nonrecognized subsequent event that may require disclosure (ASC 855). Held-for-sale or discontinued classification depends on criteria met at year-end, which were not met here.

questions.q: Which of the following would an auditor ordinarily consider the most reliable audit evidence about a client's year-end cash balance?
choices: The client's year-end bank reconciliation prepared by the controller
A photocopy of the year-end bank statement provided by the client
An oral statement by the treasurer about the balance
A confirmation sent by the auditor and returned directly to the auditor by the bank
questions.exp: AU-C 500 indicates that evidence from an independent external source, obtained directly by the auditor and in documentary form, is generally the most reliable. A client-provided copy has passed through the client's hands and could have been altered, and oral representations are the weakest.

questions.q: An auditor selects a sample of entries from the sales journal and examines the related customer orders, shipping documents, and invoices. This procedure provides evidence primarily about which assertion?
choices: Completeness
Classification
Occurrence
Cutoff
questions.exp: Vouching from recorded entries back to supporting documents tests whether the recorded transactions actually occurred. Completeness requires the opposite direction, from source documents forward to the records.

questions.q: To test the completeness of recorded purchases, which procedure is most effective?
choices: Select entries from the purchases journal and vouch them to vendor invoices
Confirm year-end accounts payable balances for vendors with the largest balances
Recompute the extensions and footings on a sample of vendor invoices
Select receiving reports and trace them to recorded entries in the purchases journal
questions.exp: Completeness is tested by starting from evidence that a transaction occurred (receiving reports) and tracing forward to see that it was recorded. Vouching recorded entries tests occurrence. Confirming only large balances misses vendors whose liabilities were left unrecorded.

questions.q: An auditor is designing a substantive analytical procedure for sales commission expense. Which of the following would most improve the precision of the auditor's expectation?
choices: Using an industry average of commissions as a percentage of revenue
Raising the acceptable difference threshold to reduce the number of items requiring investigation
Using the prior-year annual total adjusted for overall inflation
Developing the expectation monthly by sales region, using the commission rate applied to independently tested regional sales
questions.exp: AU-C 520 indicates that disaggregated data, such as monthly and by location, and reliable, independently tested inputs make an expectation more precise. A higher threshold reduces the work but makes the procedure less precise.

questions.q: In performing a substantive analytical procedure on payroll expense, the auditor finds that the recorded amount exceeds the expectation by more than the acceptable threshold. Management explains that a mid-year union contract increased wage rates. The auditor should
choices: propose an adjustment for the entire difference
conclude that the procedure was poorly designed and switch to a different procedure
corroborate management's explanation with other audit evidence, such as inspecting the union contract and testing its effect on the expectation
accept management's explanation, because it is plausible
questions.exp: AU-C 520 requires the auditor to investigate significant differences by inquiring of management and obtaining appropriate evidence relevant to the response. An uncorroborated explanation is not sufficient, and the difference is not automatically a misstatement.

questions.q: A client's long-term note payable was $6,000,000 on January 1 and $10,000,000 on December 31, with borrowings occurring evenly through the year at a fixed 6% rate. Recorded interest expense is $520,000, and the auditor's acceptable difference threshold is $25,000. What should the auditor conclude?
choices: Expected interest is $480,000, and the $40,000 difference exceeds the threshold and must be investigated
Expected interest is $360,000, and the difference cannot be evaluated without confirming the note
Expected interest is $600,000, so recorded interest is understated by $80,000
Expected interest is $480,000, and the difference is within the threshold, so no further work is needed
questions.exp: Average debt is ($6,000,000 + $10,000,000) / 2 = $8,000,000, and $8,000,000 x 6% = $480,000. The $40,000 difference exceeds the $25,000 threshold, so it must be investigated. Using the ending balance gives $600,000 and ignores the timing of the borrowings.

questions.q: An auditor reads a client's loan agreement to determine the principal due within twelve months of the balance sheet date and compares it with the current portion of long-term debt reported. This procedure most directly addresses which assertion?
choices: Accuracy
Existence
Completeness
Classification
questions.exp: Determining whether debt is properly split between current and noncurrent liabilities addresses classification and presentation. The loan's existence is better evidenced by confirmation with the lender.

questions.q: A client holds goods on consignment for other companies in its warehouse. The auditor reads consignment agreements and confirms that these goods were excluded from the client's year-end inventory. This procedure primarily addresses which assertion for inventory?
choices: Valuation and allocation
Completeness
Rights and obligations
Presentation
questions.exp: Goods held on consignment belong to the consignor, so excluding them addresses whether the entity holds rights to the recorded inventory. Completeness would address omitted goods the client does own.

questions.q: An auditor examines shipping documents for the last five business days of the year and the first five business days of the following year and compares the shipment dates with the dates sales were recorded. This procedure primarily tests
choices: valuation of accounts receivable
cutoff of sales
classification of sales
rights to accounts receivable
questions.exp: Comparing shipment dates with recording dates around year-end tests whether sales are recorded in the correct period, which is the cutoff assertion. Valuation of receivables involves collectibility, which this procedure does not address.

questions.q: An auditor compares the recorded cost of slow-moving inventory items with their selling prices after year-end, less estimated costs to complete and sell. This procedure most directly addresses which assertion?
choices: Rights and obligations
Cutoff
Existence
Valuation and allocation
questions.exp: Comparing cost with net realizable value tests whether inventory is stated at the lower of cost and NRV, which is the valuation assertion. Existence is tested by observing the physical count.

questions.q: Management refuses to let the auditor send a positive confirmation to the company's largest customer, which accounts for a material portion of receivables. Under AU-C 505, the auditor should
choices: immediately withdraw from the engagement
issue an adverse opinion on the financial statements
send the confirmation anyway, because confirmation of receivables is required
inquire about management's reasons, evaluate their validity and the implications for risk assessment, and perform alternative procedures to obtain relevant and reliable evidence
questions.exp: AU-C 505 requires the auditor to inquire about the reasons, seek evidence of their validity, consider the implications, and perform alternative procedures. If the refusal is unreasonable or alternative evidence cannot be obtained, the auditor communicates with those charged with governance and considers the effect on the opinion.

questions.q: An auditor receives no response to a second request for a positive confirmation of a material customer balance. No exceptions or fraud risks have been noted. Which procedure is most appropriate?
choices: Treat the entire balance as a misstatement
Accept the balance as confirmed, because the customer did not dispute it
Examine cash receipts after year-end and supporting shipping documents and invoices for the balance
Send a negative confirmation to replace the positive request
questions.exp: AU-C 505 requires alternative procedures for nonresponses to positive confirmations. Subsequent cash receipts and shipping documents are common sources of evidence for receivables. A nonresponse is not the same as an agreement, and a negative confirmation would provide even less evidence.

questions.q: To evaluate a client's year-end warranty liability, an auditor examines warranty claims actually paid during the two months after year-end, before the report date. Under AU-C 540, this procedure is an example of
choices: performing a retrospective review of prior-year estimates
testing the operating effectiveness of controls over the estimate
developing an auditor's point estimate independent of management
obtaining audit evidence from events occurring up to the date of the auditor's report
questions.exp: AU-C 540 identifies three approaches: obtaining evidence from events up to the report date, testing how management made the estimate, and developing an auditor's point estimate or range. Examining actual claims paid after year-end is the first approach. A retrospective review looks back at the prior year's estimates instead.

questions.q: Under AU-C 540, the auditor reviews the outcome of accounting estimates included in the prior-period financial statements. What is the primary purpose of this retrospective review?
choices: To determine whether the prior-year financial statements should be restated
To question the reasonableness of the prior-period judgments based on information now available
To determine the amount of the current-year estimate
To help identify and assess risks of material misstatement in the current period, including indications of possible management bias and the effectiveness of the estimation process
questions.exp: The retrospective review informs the current-period risk assessment and can reveal management bias or weaknesses in the estimation process. It is not intended to second-guess judgments that were reasonable given the information available at the time.

questions.q: The auditor identifies a significant transaction outside the entity's normal course of business with a company controlled by the CEO's brother. Under AU-C 550, which procedure is required?
choices: Determine the fair value of the transaction and record an adjustment for any difference
Confirm the terms of the transaction with the CEO only
Report the transaction to the SEC as a potential illegal act
Inspect the underlying contracts or agreements, evaluate the business rationale, and obtain evidence that the transaction was appropriately authorized and approved
questions.exp: For significant related party transactions outside the normal course of business, AU-C 550 requires inspecting the underlying agreements, evaluating the business rationale, checking that the terms agree with management's explanations, and obtaining evidence of authorization and approval. Confirming only with the interested party is not appropriate.

questions.q: A client's outside legal counsel, which has devoted substantive attention to several pending lawsuits, refuses to respond to the auditor's inquiry letter. Under AU-C 501, the lawyer's refusal ordinarily
choices: is a limitation on the scope of the audit sufficient to preclude an unmodified opinion
should be treated as an indication that the lawsuits are immaterial
has no effect, because management's representations about litigation are sufficient
requires an emphasis-of-matter paragraph
questions.exp: Inquiry of legal counsel is the auditor's primary means of corroborating management's information about litigation, claims, and assessments. A lawyer's refusal to furnish the requested information ordinarily is a scope limitation that precludes an unmodified opinion. Management's representations do not replace the lawyer's response.

questions.q: Which of the following events occurring after the balance sheet date but before the financial statements are issued would require an adjustment to the financial statements?
choices: A lawsuit that arose from an accident before year-end is settled for an amount significantly larger than the amount accrued
The company issues a large amount of new common stock after year-end
The company acquires a competitor after year-end
A fire destroys a warehouse two weeks after year-end
questions.exp: A settlement that provides additional evidence about a condition existing at the balance sheet date is a recognized (Type 1) subsequent event requiring adjustment. A fire, a stock issuance, or an acquisition after year-end reflects a new condition and may require disclosure only.

questions.q: Which of the following procedures would an auditor most likely perform to identify subsequent events between the date of the financial statements and the date of the auditor's report?
choices: Observe the physical inventory count at year-end
Read minutes of meetings of shareholders, directors, and committees held after year-end
Recompute depreciation expense for the year
Confirm year-end accounts receivable with customers
questions.exp: AU-C 560 requires procedures such as inquiring of management, reading minutes of meetings held after year-end, and reading the latest interim financial statements. The other procedures relate to year-end balances, not to events after year-end.

questions.q: After the auditor's report has been released, the auditor learns that a large receivable was uncollectible at year-end because the customer was already bankrupt. This fact would have changed the report had it been known. Under AU-C 560, the auditor should first
choices: discuss the matter with management and, as appropriate, those charged with governance, and determine whether the financial statements need revision
take no action, because the auditor has no responsibility after the report release date
withdraw the report without discussion with management
notify regulatory authorities and all users of the financial statements
questions.exp: For subsequently discovered facts that existed at the report date, AU-C 560 requires discussion with management and those charged with governance and a determination of whether revision is needed. Only if management fails to take the necessary steps does the auditor act to prevent future reliance on the report.

questions.q: The auditor completed fieldwork and dated the report March 1. On March 10, before the report was released, a significant event occurred and was disclosed in Note 12 to the financial statements. The auditor does not want to extend procedures on other subsequent events beyond March 1. How should the report be dated?
choices: The date the report is released to the client
March 10
March 1
March 1, except for Note 12, as to which the date is March 10
questions.exp: Dual dating limits the auditor's responsibility for events after the original date to the specific matter disclosed. Using March 10 alone would extend the auditor's subsequent events responsibility for all matters to that date. Keeping March 1 alone would not cover the new disclosure.

questions.q: Under AU-C 580, the management representation letter should be dated
choices: as near as practicable to, but not after, the date of the auditor's report
as of the balance sheet date
as of the date the auditor's report is released
as of the last day of fieldwork, which may be before the report date
questions.exp: AU-C 580 requires written representations to be dated as near as practicable to, but not after, the date of the auditor's report, and to cover all periods referred to in the report. The balance sheet date is too early to cover subsequent events.

questions.q: Management refuses to provide written representations acknowledging its responsibility for the preparation and fair presentation of the financial statements. Under AU-C 580, the auditor should
choices: disclaim an opinion or withdraw from the engagement
obtain oral representations instead
issue an unmodified opinion with an emphasis-of-matter paragraph
issue a qualified opinion
questions.exp: Representations about management's responsibilities are so fundamental that their absence requires a disclaimer of opinion or withdrawal under AU-C 580. A qualified opinion is not enough for this pervasive problem.

questions.q: Which statement about the sufficiency and appropriateness of audit evidence is correct?
choices: Obtaining more audit evidence may not compensate for its poor quality
Sufficiency is unaffected by the assessed risk of material misstatement
Obtaining a larger quantity of evidence always compensates for evidence of poor quality
Appropriateness refers only to the quantity of evidence obtained
questions.exp: AU-C 500 explains that sufficiency is the quantity of evidence and appropriateness is its quality (relevance and reliability). More evidence may not compensate for poor quality. The amount needed increases with the assessed RMM, so sufficiency is affected by risk.

questions.q: Under AU-C 230, the auditor should assemble the final audit file and complete the administrative process no later than
choices: 90 days after the balance sheet date
45 days after the report release date
60 days after the report release date
14 days after the report release date
questions.exp: GAAS sets the documentation completion date at no later than 60 days after the report release date, and documentation is retained for at least five years. The 45-day period applies under PCAOB AS 1215.

questions.q: After the documentation completion date, an auditor needs to add an explanatory memo to the audit file. Under AU-C 230, which is correct?
choices: The auditor may add documentation but must not delete or discard any, and must document when, by whom, and why the changes were made
The auditor may replace the original documentation with an updated version
No changes of any kind may be made after the documentation completion date
The auditor may delete superseded documentation as long as it is not needed to support the report
questions.exp: After the documentation completion date, AU-C 230 allows additions but forbids deleting or discarding documentation before the end of the retention period. The auditor must record the nature of the change, who made it and when, and the reason.

questions.q: In testing journal entries for evidence of management override as required by AU-C 240, which entry would the auditor most likely select for testing?
choices: A recurring entry that records monthly rent expense
A round-dollar entry to a seldom-used account, posted by a senior executive after the year-end close
A recurring monthly depreciation entry generated automatically by the fixed asset system
A standard payroll entry posted by the payroll clerk on the regular payroll date
questions.exp: AU-C 240 directs the auditor to select entries with fraud risk characteristics, such as unusual accounts, individuals who do not normally post entries, round amounts, and entries posted at or after period-end. Routine, system-generated entries have a lower risk of being used for override.

questions.q: During the client's physical inventory count, an auditor wants evidence that inventory recorded on the count sheets actually exists. The auditor should
choices: select items on the warehouse floor and trace them to the count sheets
compare the total count with the prior-year inventory balance
select items from the count sheets and locate and count them physically
inquire of warehouse personnel whether all items were counted
questions.exp: Testing from the records to the physical items supports existence. Testing from the floor to the count sheets supports completeness, so the direction of the test is the key distinction.

questions.q: An auditor plans to use a system-generated aged accounts receivable report as the basis for testing the allowance for credit losses. Under AU-C 500, the auditor should
choices: evaluate whether the information is sufficiently reliable, including obtaining evidence about its accuracy and completeness
use the report only if it is printed in the auditor's presence
use the report without further consideration, because it was generated by the system
obtain management's written representation that the report is accurate
questions.exp: AU-C 500 requires the auditor to evaluate whether information produced by the entity is reliable enough for the auditor's purposes, including its accuracy and completeness, for example by testing the aging logic and reconciling the report to the ledger. System generation and management representations do not establish reliability by themselves.

questions.q: Management engaged an external actuary to calculate its pension obligation, and the auditor plans to use the actuary's report as audit evidence. Under AU-C 500, the auditor should
choices: re-engage the same actuary as the auditor's specialist
refer to the actuary in the auditor's report to share responsibility
evaluate the competence, capabilities, and objectivity of management's specialist, obtain an understanding of the specialist's work, and evaluate the appropriateness of that work as audit evidence
accept the report without further procedures, because actuaries are licensed professionals
questions.exp: AU-C 500 requires these procedures when using the work of a management's specialist as audit evidence. A professional license alone does not establish objectivity or appropriateness, and the auditor's report never refers to a management's specialist.

questions.q: An auditor wants evidence that the duties of opening mail, recording cash receipts, and reconciling the bank account are performed by different employees. This control leaves no documentary trail. Which approach provides the most appropriate evidence of its operating effectiveness?
choices: Inquiry combined with observation of the employees performing their assigned duties
Inquiry of the controller about who performs each duty
Recalculation of the cash receipts totals for a sample of days
Inspection of the bank reconciliations for the reviewer's initials
questions.exp: For a control with no documentation, such as segregation of duties, the auditor combines inquiry with observation and, where possible, corroborating inquiry. AU-C 330 states that inquiry alone is not sufficient to test operating effectiveness. Inspecting reconciliation initials tests a different control.

questions.q: To test a credit approval control, an auditor selects a sample of approved sales orders, independently obtains each customer's credit limit and outstanding balance at the order date, and determines whether the approval was appropriate under company policy. This procedure is best described as
choices: inspection
reperformance
inquiry
observation
questions.exp: Reperformance means the auditor independently executes the control to see whether it was performed properly. It provides stronger evidence than inspecting for approval initials, which shows only that someone signed, not that the approval was appropriate.

questions.q: An auditor tested the operating effectiveness of controls over purchasing as of September 30 and plans to rely on them for the year ending December 31. Under AU-C 330, the auditor should
choices: retest the controls as of December 31 using the same sample size
make no further inquiry, because interim testing covers the entire year
obtain evidence about significant changes to the controls after the interim date and determine what additional evidence is needed for the remaining period
assess control risk at the maximum for the fourth quarter
questions.exp: When controls are tested at an interim date, AU-C 330 requires the auditor to obtain evidence about significant changes after that date and to determine the additional evidence needed for the remaining period. That judgment considers factors such as the significance of the RMM, the length of the remaining period, and the control environment. A full retest is not automatically required.

questions.q: An auditor tested a manual control over payroll rate changes in the prior-year audit. The control does not address a significant risk. In the current year, inquiry combined with inspection of documentation shows that the control has not changed. Under AU-C 330, the auditor
choices: may rely on the prior-year evidence only if management represents in writing that the control is unchanged
must retest the control in the current year, because evidence from prior audits cannot be used
may rely on the prior-year evidence, provided each such control is tested at least once in every third audit and some controls are tested in each audit
may rely on the prior-year evidence indefinitely as long as the control remains unchanged
questions.exp: AU-C 330 allows evidence from prior audits for unchanged controls not addressing significant risks if continuing relevance is established. Such controls must be tested at least once every third audit, with some controls tested in each audit. Indefinite reliance and reliance on representations alone are not permitted.

questions.q: An auditor plans to rely on controls over revenue recognition for a contract type the auditor has identified as a significant risk. The same controls were tested last year and have not changed. Under AU-C 330, the auditor
choices: need not test the controls, because significant risks are addressed only by substantive procedures
may rely on last year's test if this is not the third consecutive audit
must test the operating effectiveness of those controls in the current period
may rely on last year's test, because the controls have not changed
questions.exp: AU-C 330 prohibits relying on evidence from previous audits for controls that mitigate a significant risk. If the auditor relies on those controls, they must be tested in the current period. Significant risks may be addressed partly through controls, so it is wrong to say that only substantive procedures apply.

questions.q: From a sample of cash disbursement vouchers, an auditor examines each voucher for evidence of approval by an authorized manager and also agrees the amount paid to the vendor invoice and receiving report. This approach is best described as
choices: a walkthrough
a substantive analytical procedure
a dual-purpose test
a test of controls only
questions.exp: A dual-purpose test uses the same items to test a control (approval) and to perform a test of details (agreeing amounts). The sample must be large enough to meet the objectives of both tests. A walkthrough follows one or a few transactions through the process to confirm understanding.

questions.q: While testing approval of journal entries, an auditor finds one deviation: the controller bypassed the required CFO approval to post a large entry that reduced an accrued liability, and the controller cannot explain why. How should the auditor treat this deviation?
choices: Disregard it, because one deviation in a sample is within the expected rate
Replace the item with another selection, because the deviation was unusual
Consider its qualitative implications, including possible fraud and management override, beyond its effect on the deviation rate
Evaluate it only by including it in the computed sample deviation rate
questions.exp: AU-C 530 and AU-C 240 require the auditor to consider the nature and cause of deviations. An apparently intentional override by management may indicate fraud and affect the risk assessment and the reliability of representations, regardless of the deviation rate. Replacing the item would hide the problem.

questions.q: Under PCAOB AS 2201, an auditor tested an automated control that calculates sales discounts and established a baseline in a prior year. In the current year, which condition allows the auditor to use a benchmarking strategy rather than retesting the control's operation?
choices: Benchmarking is allowed for manual controls but not automated controls
Management represents that no program changes were made during the year
The control was tested in the prior year with no exceptions, regardless of the IT general controls
IT general controls, including program change controls, are effective and the auditor verifies that the control has not changed since the baseline was established
questions.exp: AS 2201 allows benchmarking of automated application controls when IT general controls, especially program change and access controls, are effective and the auditor verifies that the control has not changed. A representation from management or a clean prior-year result alone is not enough.

questions.q: A user entity's year ends December 31. The service organization's SOC 1 Type 2 report covers January 1 through September 30. To rely on the service organization's controls for the full year, the user auditor should
choices: rely on the report without further procedures, because nine months is most of the year
request that the service auditor reissue the report with a December 31 date
disregard the report entirely, because it does not cover the year-end date

obtain additional evidence about the October-December period, such as inquiries of the service organization about significant changes (for example, through a bridge letter), considering the length of the uncovered period and the degree of reliance
questions.exp: AU-C 402 requires the user auditor to determine what additional evidence is needed for periods outside the report, considering the length of the gap and the degree of reliance. Bridge letters and inquiries are common sources. The report is still useful evidence, so disregarding it is not necessary.

questions.q: A user auditor plans to rely on controls at a payroll service organization to reduce substantive testing of payroll expense. The only report available is a SOC 1 Type 1 report. Which statement is correct?
choices: The Type 1 report is not relevant to a financial statement audit
The Type 1 report allows reliance if the user auditor refers to the service auditor in the audit report

The Type 1 report addresses the fairness of the description and the suitability of design at a point in time, but not operating effectiveness, so the auditor needs other evidence to rely on the controls
The Type 1 report provides sufficient evidence of operating effectiveness for the full year
questions.exp: A Type 1 report covers the description and the design of controls as of a specified date. Only a Type 2 report includes tests of operating effectiveness over a period. To rely on controls, the user auditor must obtain a Type 2 report or perform or arrange other tests (AU-C 402).

questions.q: A SOC 1 Type 2 report states that the service organization's controls achieve their objectives only if user entities reconcile the monthly payroll registers to their own time records. Under AU-C 402, the user auditor should
choices: ignore the statement, because it is the service auditor's responsibility
rely on the service auditor's opinion, which covers user entity controls
report the matter as a material weakness of the service organization
obtain an understanding of and, if relying on the controls, test the user entity's complementary user entity controls
questions.exp: Complementary user entity controls (CUECs) are controls the service organization assumes user entities will have. The service auditor does not test them, so the user auditor must evaluate them at the user entity and test them if relying on the controls.

questions.q: A service organization's SOC 1 Type 2 report uses the carve-out method for a subservice organization that hosts its applications. What does this mean for the user auditor?
choices: The subservice organization's controls were tested by the service auditor and included in the opinion
The user auditor must disclaim an opinion on the user entity's financial statements
The subservice organization's relevant controls are excluded from the description and testing, so the user auditor must consider how to obtain evidence about them
The subservice organization's controls are not relevant to the user entity's financial reporting
questions.exp: Under the carve-out method, the subservice organization's controls are excluded from the description and from the service auditor's tests. The user auditor may need a separate report on the subservice organization or other evidence. The inclusive method would include those controls.

questions.q: A user auditor relied on a SOC 1 Type 2 report from a service organization and is issuing an unmodified opinion. Under AU-C 402, the user auditor's report
choices: should refer to the service auditor's report to indicate shared responsibility
should not refer to the work of the service auditor
should refer to the service auditor only if the service auditor's report contained exceptions
should include the service auditor's report as an attachment
questions.exp: AU-C 402 prohibits a user auditor from referring to the service auditor's work in an unmodified opinion unless law or regulation requires it. If a reference is relevant to explaining a modification, the report must state that it does not reduce the user auditor's responsibility.

questions.q: In an integrated audit of an issuer, the auditor tests controls to support both the opinion on internal control over financial reporting and reliance in the financial statement audit. Which statement about the period of testing is correct?
choices: Controls need be tested only at the beginning of the year for the ICFR opinion
Testing at any interim date is sufficient for both purposes, without roll-forward procedures
Testing only during the last week of the year is sufficient for financial statement reliance throughout the year
Tests should provide evidence that controls are effective as of year-end for the ICFR opinion and throughout the period of reliance for the financial statement audit
questions.exp: Under AS 2201, the ICFR opinion is as of the end of the period, while control reliance in the financial statement audit requires evidence over the period of reliance. Integrated testing is designed to meet both objectives. Interim testing needs roll-forward procedures to reach year-end.

questions.q: Which of the following would most likely increase the extent of an auditor's tests of operating effectiveness for a manual control?
choices: The auditor plans to perform extensive substantive tests of the related account regardless of the control's effectiveness
The auditor expects no deviations based on prior-year results
The control is performed once a year rather than daily
The auditor plans to rely heavily on the control to reduce the extent of substantive procedures
questions.exp: Greater planned reliance on a control requires more persuasive evidence of its effectiveness, so the extent of testing increases (AU-C 330). Annual controls need fewer test items than daily controls, and a low expected deviation rate reduces sample size.

questions.q: An auditor is testing management's monthly review of operating expense variances by department as a control over the completeness of accruals. Which procedure is most important to the test?
choices: Asking the reviewer whether any variances were found during the year
Inspecting the reports for the reviewer's signature only
Evaluating the precision of the review, including the investigation thresholds and follow-up, and testing the completeness and accuracy of the information used in the review
Confirming that the monthly review meeting appears on the controller's calendar
questions.exp: For management review controls, the auditor evaluates whether the review is precise enough to detect material misstatements and tests the reliability of the information produced by the entity that the review uses. A signature shows only that the review happened, not that it was effective.

questions.q: An auditor is testing a control designed to ensure that every shipment to a customer is billed. From which population should the auditor select items for testing?
choices: Entries in the accounts receivable subsidiary ledger
Shipping documents prepared by the shipping department
Sales invoices recorded in the sales journal
Customer purchase orders received
questions.exp: To test completeness of billing, the auditor starts from evidence that shipments occurred (shipping documents) and traces them forward to invoices. Selecting from recorded invoices could never reveal a shipment that was not billed.

questions.q: Company policy requires a manager's initials on each vendor invoice before payment. In testing this control, the auditor finds an invoice that was paid without initials, although the auditor confirms that the goods were received and the price was correct. The auditor should treat this item as
choices: a deviation only if the amount exceeds the clearly trivial threshold
a monetary misstatement in accounts payable
not a deviation, because the transaction was valid
a deviation from the prescribed control
questions.exp: A test of controls evaluates whether the control was performed as prescribed. The absence of required approval is a deviation, even if the underlying transaction turns out to be valid. The validity of the transaction relates to substantive testing, not to whether the control operated.

questions.q: While testing controls over cash disbursements using a sample, the auditor cannot locate the supporting documentation for one selected voucher, and no alternative procedure can determine whether the control was applied. Under AU-C 530, the auditor should
choices: treat the item as a deviation
select a replacement voucher and continue testing
rely on the clerk's statement that the voucher was properly approved
exclude the item from the sample and reduce the sample size by one
questions.exp: AU-C 530 says that when the auditor cannot apply the designed procedures or suitable alternatives to a selected item, the item is treated as a deviation. Replacement is appropriate only for items that are not applicable, such as a properly voided check, not for missing documentation.

questions.q: What is the primary limitation of observation as a test of controls?
choices: Observation cannot be used for controls that involve segregation of duties
Observation produces documentary evidence that is too costly to retain
Observation is considered less reliable than inquiry
The evidence relates only to the point in time when the observation was made, and employees may act differently when observed
questions.exp: Observation shows how a control is performed when the auditor is present, but it gives limited evidence about other times in the period, and people may behave differently while observed. Observation is actually a key procedure for segregation of duties and is more reliable than inquiry alone.

questions.q: An auditor attends an unannounced distribution of paychecks and requires each employee to show identification before receiving a check. The auditor then follows up on any unclaimed checks. This procedure is primarily designed to provide evidence that
choices: employees' pay rates are properly authorized
employees on the payroll actually exist and are working for the company
payroll taxes are withheld correctly
overtime hours are approved by supervisors
questions.exp: A surprise payroll distribution addresses the risk of fictitious employees on the payroll, which relates to occurrence or existence. Pay rate authorization and tax withholding are tested by inspecting personnel files and recalculating.

questions.q: An auditor concludes that testing controls over prepaid expenses would be less efficient than performing substantive procedures, and no significant risk exists for that area. Under AU-C 330, the auditor
choices: must still test controls over prepaid expenses before performing substantive procedures
must obtain management's written representation that controls are effective
may omit both tests of controls and substantive procedures
may choose not to test controls, assess control risk at the maximum, and perform substantive procedures responsive to the assessed risks
questions.exp: Tests of controls are required only when the auditor plans to rely on controls or when substantive procedures alone cannot provide sufficient evidence. Otherwise, the auditor may use a substantive approach with control risk assessed at the maximum. Substantive procedures are still required for material balances.

questions.q: Under AU-C 330, in designing tests of operating effectiveness, the auditor should obtain evidence about which of the following?
choices: How the control was applied at relevant times during the period, the consistency with which it was applied, and by whom or by what means it was applied
Only whether the control exists at year-end
Only whether management believes the control is effective
Only whether the control was documented in the entity's policies manual
questions.exp: AU-C 330 directs tests of operating effectiveness to how the control was applied during the period, the consistency of its application, and by whom or by what means. Existence at a point in time or in a policy manual addresses design and implementation, not operation.

questions.q: On July 1, a client replaced its manual three-way match with an automated matching control. The auditor plans to rely on controls over the matching of purchase documents for the entire calendar year. The auditor should
choices: test both the manual control for January through June and the automated control for July through December
test only the automated control, because it is in place at year-end
test only the manual control, because it operated for the longest period
assess control risk at the maximum, because controls that change mid-year cannot be relied on
questions.exp: To rely on controls for the whole period, the auditor needs evidence about each control that operated during the period of reliance. That means testing the superseded manual control and the new automated control. Testing only the year-end control would leave the first half of the year without support.

questions.q: An auditor is testing an automated application control that calculates depreciation using the asset's recorded life and method. IT general controls have been tested and found effective. What extent of testing of the automated control itself is generally sufficient?
choices: A sample of at least 60 assets, as for a daily manual control
Testing every asset in the fixed asset register
Testing one instance of each relevant type of calculation or condition the control processes
No testing, because IT general controls are effective
questions.exp: Because computers process consistently, an automated control supported by effective ITGCs can be tested with one instance of each relevant condition or calculation type. Effective ITGCs support continued operation, but they do not replace testing the application control itself at least once.

questions.q: The external auditor plans to use the internal audit function's tests of controls over inventory as audit evidence. Under AU-C 610, which procedure must the external auditor perform?
choices: Reperform all of the internal auditors' tests
Perform sufficient procedures on the body of the internal audit work it plans to use, including reperformance of some of that work
Refer to the internal audit function in the auditor's report
Accept the internal audit results, provided the internal audit director signs a representation
questions.exp: AU-C 610 requires the external auditor to perform procedures on the body of internal audit work it plans to use, including reperformance of some of it, to evaluate its adequacy. Full reperformance is not required, and the auditor's report never refers to the internal audit function.

questions.q: An auditor did not test controls over sales, but extensive substantive tests of details found no misstatements in revenue. Which conclusion about the controls over sales is appropriate?
choices: The controls are operating effectively, because no misstatements were found
The controls should be reported as a significant deficiency
The absence of misstatements found by substantive procedures does not provide evidence that the controls are operating effectively
The controls may be relied on in the next year without testing
questions.exp: AU-C 330 notes that the absence of misstatements found by substantive procedures is not evidence that the related controls are effective. A misstatement found substantively may, however, indicate a control deficiency. Controls must be tested directly before they can be relied on.

questions.q: A user auditor auditing a company's financial statements receives a SOC 2 Type 2 report from the company's cloud service provider. The report is primarily designed to address
choices: controls relevant to security, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality, or privacy based on the trust services criteria
the user entity's complementary controls
controls relevant to user entities' internal control over financial reporting
the fairness of the service organization's financial statements
questions.exp: SOC 2 reports address controls relevant to the trust services criteria. They may provide useful information, but SOC 1 reports are designed for user entities' internal control over financial reporting and for user auditors. Mixing up SOC 1 and SOC 2 is the common trap.

questions.q: Company policy requires that credit memos be issued only for goods actually returned, as evidenced by a receiving report for returned goods. Which test of controls best supports reliance on this policy?
choices: Confirm year-end accounts receivable balances with customers
Select credit memos issued during the year and inspect them for supporting receiving reports for the returned goods
Select receiving reports for returned goods and trace them to the inventory records
Inquire of the sales manager about the credit memo approval process
questions.exp: The risk is credit memos without actual returns, so the auditor starts from the credit memos and looks for support. Tracing receiving reports to inventory tests a different direction, which is completeness of recording returns, and inquiry alone is not enough.

questions.q: An auditor plans to rely on a control requiring that changes to employee pay rates in the payroll master file be authorized in writing by the human resources department. Which test of controls is most appropriate?
choices: Compare total payroll expense with the prior year
Observe the payroll clerk processing the current week's time cards
Recompute gross pay for a sample of employees using current pay rates
Select changes from a system-generated report of master file pay rate changes, test the report's completeness, and inspect for HR's written authorization
questions.exp: The control operates on master file changes, so the population should be the changes made during the period, drawn from a report whose completeness the auditor tests, with each change inspected for authorization. Recomputing pay with current rates would not reveal unauthorized rates.
